Attribut.Explanation: "It’s about your ability to fight in close combat, execute a measured strike, and your effectiveness in the tumult of a free-for-all. This Attribute is also used for unarmed combat, when the weapon is your own body !"

"It represents your ability to hit targets with ranged weapons such as bows and throwing knives, and in general throwing objects. This Attribute is also used as the basis for other ranged attacks such as Troll’s Vomit."
"This indicates how much Damage you do in Melee, how much you can lift, and how good you are at Swimming and Climbing."
"It’s about your physical stamina. It helps you survive damage in combat, but also harsh conditions and resist poison."

"It represents your speed of thought and reaction, especially in the heat of the moment and when you are under pressure. It determines the order of battle, your intuition and perception, and helps you be the first to react."
"Agility is the expression of your physical coordination and your natural athletic abilities, the basis in areas such as running, riding and concealment. It is also used to dodge blows in combat."
"It indicates your ability to perform delicate manual tasks such as playing a musical instrument or skillfully crafting objects. She also helps you with sleight of hand or picking pockets."
"Intelligence symbolizes the potential for thought, analysis and understanding. Useful for healing, evaluating and for knowledge in general, it is essential for understanding and casting spells."

"Willpower represents your overall willpower and ability to ignore difficulties and focus on the work at hand. It helps to resist all kinds of influences and coercions, and protects against fear and terror."

"Sociability causes you to get along with people and appear quite pleasant and decent. She helps you when talking to locals or commanding people in combat, cajoling guards or trying to bribe them, and, for pious Characters, when communicating with your deity."

"Your Wound Points indicate the amount of Damage you can sustain based on your physical power and willpower to avoid injury. See Chapter 5: Rules for more on how to use Wound Points to calculate Damage. This indicates how much Damage you do in Melee, how much you can lift, and how good you are at Swimming and Climbing. Determine Wounds. Unlike other Attributes, Wound Points are calculated from your Characteristics, more ifically your Strength, Endurance and Mental Strength Bonuses (abbreviations BF, BE and BFM in the Attributes Table). Simply locate the appropriate Bonuses on your Character Sheet and add them together to determine your Wound Points. Note: Halflings automatically have the Small Talent and start with less Wound Points (see page 343)."
"Your Destiny represents your future and is directly linked to your Luck"

"your Resilience corresponds to your inner strength, defined by your Determination. Your Resilience also comes with a Motivation. Your Motivation can be defined by a single word or phrase describing what drives your Character forward. See page 170 for more information on this. Choose Motivation. All Characters choose a Motivation that represents their very essence, a word or phrase that sums up what they live for, or what keeps them going. Although it is an obvious advantage for the interpretation of your Character, Motivation is also used to help you regain Resolve Points. When considering your Motivation, think of a defining characteristic, something essential to the nature of your Character. Also try to make it fun to play and compatible with other PCs and their own Motivations."
"Additional Points to Place Between Fate and Resilience"

"Motion is used to determine your walking and running speeds. The standard Human Movement is 4. If you are using a grid for movement, this indicates the number of squares you can move in one Round, or centimeters on a table. In the longer term, it indicates how many kilometers per hour you can easily cover on foot. For more details on Movement, see page 164."

Skill.Explanation: "This is your ability to befriend, quickly calm, or enslave animals. A successful Animal Control Test allows you to influence the behavior of one or more animals, up to a maximum equal to your Mental Strength Bonus + DR. If the animal targets are naturally docile, this Test may be uncontested, but is usually opposed to the target’s Mental Strength. In combat, you can use Animal Grip when fighting animals. If you succeed, no affected target will attack you this Round and you gain +1 Advantage. You can do this for as many successive Rounds as you like, until you decide to stop or fail an Animal Control Test. After which the instinct of the creature takes over and you no longer have any influence."

"Create works of art with the medium of your choice. Not having access to the appropriate Tools of the Profession will result in a penalty to your Tests. The DR obtained determines the quality of the final work. An Extended Test may be required for the completion of a complex or large work of art. The Art Skill is little used in combat, but marble busts can make great improvised weapons. Example: Irina has been commissioned to paint the portrait of a local noble, whose favor her group is seeking. Its GM decides that it requires a total of 10 DRs on an Extended Art Test, and each Test represents one week of work."
"This is your ability to run, jump, move with speed and grace, and perform any general physical activity. Refer to Movement (see page 164) for more details on using Athletics in combat movement."

"The Calm Skill allows you to stay calm under pressure, resist fear when faced with horror, and stick to your convictions. Calm is generally used to resist other Skills – Charm, Intimidate and similar Skills – but you may also need to make a Calm Test against something that forces you to act against your will. Calm is also the main Skill used to resist the effects of Psychology (see page 190)."

"Charm makes people think highly of you, your views, and your proposed actions. Passing an opposed Charm/Calm Test allows you to influence the attitude of one or more targets, up to a maximum equal to your Sociability Bonus + DR, affecting the target with the lowest Mental Strength first. If a target is favorable to your Charm, the Test will be uncontested. - BEG: The Charm Skill can be used to beg in the streets. A successful Test will earn you a number of copper coins equal to your Sociability Bonus x DR per hour from passers-by, the Difficulty of which is modified by the speech chosen to beg and how sympathetic your appearance can be. If you don’t roll a DR, but still pass the Test, you only manage to get a penny. A Staggering Failure (-6) means that you may have gotten into trouble with the local guards, or with other local beggars, or suffered major failures. Note: Characters caught begging by their peers or associates will likely lose their Status, unless they already have a Beggar Career, or another Career with no resources. - PUBLIC SPEAKING: The Charm Skill can be used to deliver a striking speech with the aim of tilting multiple targets in favor of your way of thinking. Assuming they can hear you and are inclined to listen to you, you can influence a number of targets equal to your Sociability Bonus + DR with a single Charm Test, influencing targets with the highest Willpower first. weak. If the crowd is unleashed, or unreceptive to your speech, the Test is set against the average Willpower of the crowd (usually 35). A failure indicates that the crowd is not convinced. The Orator and Great Orator Talents can significantly increase the number of people you affect with Charm. Rolling a Stunning Fail on a Charm Test means your audience quickly turns into an angry mob, and you are the target of their wrath. - COMBAT: Your GM may allow you to use Charm in Combat, if he thinks your enemies might be sensitive to your way of begging for your life or persuasive arguments to end the violence (good luck charming a Goblin!) If you use Charm as an Action, calculate the number of potential targets as normal. If you use it to defend yourself, the Action only affects your opponent. On a success, charmed targets will not attack you this Round and you gain +1 Advantage as normal. You can repeat the action over several Rounds until you stop or fail, after which your words will have no effect."

"This is how you master riding a particular group of animals; Ride (Horse), for example, will allow you to ride horses, mules, donkeys, and other similar animals. You will only need to Test when you want to perform something unusual, such as running, taming, traversing dangerous terrain, or charging into combat. Otherwise, if you have the Skill, you are considered able to ride without needing a Test. If you are mounted on a steed, you move using the steed’s Movement stats; if you want to run, jump, or leap, you use your Ride skill, not Athletics. An extended Ride Test may be needed if you are going somewhere, the target DR depending on the length of the trip, and the number of Tests indicating how long you take to arrive. A Ride Test can be modified by environmental conditions and the temperament of the mount. For more information on mounts, see Chapter 12: Bestiary."

"The Close Combat Skill represents the specific training you have received with a single type of close combat weapon. Each Close Combat Specialization indicates training in a specific weapon class. If you do not have the appropriate Specialization for a weapon you wish to use, refer to Chapter 11: Equipment Guide to view the weapon’s stats and find out what penalties you will incur. See Chapter 5: Rules for more information on combat and the use of the Close Combat Skill."

"This is an indication of your ability to lead others and gain respect. Most often associated with martial situations, however, a determined leader can react quickly to a fire or other disaster, and nobles frequently use the Skill to command their subordinates. A successful Command Test allows you to issue orders to a number of targets equal to your Fellowship Bonus + DR. If the targets are your direct subordinates – a noble commanding a serf or a sergeant leading his troops – the orders meet with no opposition. If there is no hierarchy in place, or the order is particularly demanding – such as ordering your soldiers to charge the head of a hydra – the Check is opposed to your targets’ Calmness. In combat, you can use Command to encourage your subordinates. A successful Leadership Test grants a +10 bonus to all Psychology Tests until the end of the next Round (see page 190). Additionally, Command can be used to transfer Boon to allies who can hear you; after a successful Leadership Test, you can transfer an Advantage to an ally of your choice, and +1 Advantage per DR obtained, which can again be allocated to allies of your choice within earshot. - Example: Lord Ludwig von Schemp watched his two bodyguards chatting with thugs for three Rounds, using his Intuition Skill to accumulate 3 Advantages. Sensing that the situation is going nowhere, he issues a peremptory order to attack the leader; Passing his Test with 5 DRs, he gives 2 Boons to one of his bodyguards and 1 Boon to the other, hoping this will end the matter quickly. - WHO IS THE BOSS ? GMs should be aware that Players giving orders to other Players can cause tension within the party. If you have Players with different social classes or military ranks, be sure to discuss how this will affect the group dynamics to ensure a smooth and enjoyable game for everyone."

"Hitch Driving allows you to drive vehicles – mostly simple wagons and heavy stagecoaches, not to mention the more “experimental“ creations of Imperial Engineers – on the roads of the Empire with as little incidents as possible. The Ride Skill can be actively used in combat. See Chapter 5: Rules for more information on mounted combat. Under normal circumstances, if you have the Driving Skill, no Test is necessary. If conditions are less than ideal – perhaps the road is bad or the weather is terrible – a Driving Test is required. If you do not have the Driving Skill, a Test may be required to perform even basic maneuvers. An Amazing Failure on a Drive Test means something bad has happened. Roll on the following table: 1–2 Broken harness: a horse (or equivalent) breaks free; reduce speed accordingly. 3–5 Road bumps: Passengers suffer 1 Wound Point and fragile cargo may be damaged. 6–8 Broken Wheel: Pass a Hitch Driving Test each Round to avoid the crash. Two-wheeled vehicles with a Broken Wheel are automatically Wrecked. 9–10 Broken Axle: Vehicle spins out of control and is damaged. Accident: Occupants of Accidented vehicles generally suffer 2d10 Wound Points modified by Endurance Bonus and AP, unless the vehicle was moving slowly (determined by the GM). Wrecked vehicles must be repaired by someone with the appropriate Trade Skill, such as Trade (Carpenter) or Trade (Wheeler). A spare tire can be installed by anyone with an appropriate Hitch Drive Test or Trade Test. In combat, Hitch Driving can be used if circumstances permit – for example, if the party is in a stagecoach being attacked by outlaws, and you wish to ram an enemy or outrun them (see page 165)."

"You know the locking mechanisms and how to open them without needing your own keys. Picking a lock often requires an Extended Test, with the number of DRs needed to open the lock depending on its complexity. - LOCKS AND PICKING TOOLS Difficulty Levels assume the use of picking tools. Improvised hooks, such as hairpins or nails, may be used with a -10 penalty. Each Test normally requires a full Round, although the GM may decide that some locks are particularly sticky or rusty, and require more time. If the GM deems a lock simple enough, non-specialized Characters may attempt a single Very Hard (-30) Dexterity Test to pick the lock. The following table shows the standard difficulties of the most common locks in the Old World. Type of lock. Difficulty. Latch: Accessible (+20) DR 0. Classic Door: Intermediate (+0) DR 2. Secure Door: Complex (-10) DR 2. Treasure Chest: Hard (-20) DR 5. Armored Door: Very Hard ( -30) DR 10."

"This Skill allows you to sneak and hide in the shadows more easily than most people. Stealth is usually opposed to your opponent’s Perception Skill, and Tests will be modified by how dark or concealed your route is, as well as how carefully you dress or not dress accordingly. An Impressive or Stunning Failure on a Stealth Test will likely immediately draw the attention of the enemies you were trying to avoid in the first place. Stealth has many potential applications in combat, most useful for concealing yourself when setting up an Ambush, or for sneaking up behind an opponent to outflank them. See Chapter 5: Rules for more information on the consequences of this action. Of course, you can also use the Skill to flee a conflict without being seen... - OPTION: SPINNING Shadowing is the act of following someone discreetly. This requires a Combined Perception and Stealth Test (see page 155). If the target is actively trying to cover their tracks, the Test is opposed to the target’s Stealth Skill. If you pass the Perception Test and fail the Stealth Test, you follow the target, but you are spotted. If you fail the Perception Test, but pass the Stealth Test, you lose your target, but go unnoticed."

"This Skill allows you to entertain crowds with words, perhaps singing, acting, or cracking a few jokes. A successful use of the Entertainment Skill means that you have amused the surrounding spectators enough to make them listen to you; the DR indicates how successful you have been. In combat, Entertainment is unlikely to be of much use, although you may find an interesting way to use Entertainment (Interpretation) to confuse or deceive your opponents."

"Training represents your understanding of a particular type of animal, and your ability to train it. A successful use of this Skill allows you to identify the Trained abilities possessed by an animal belonging to your Specialization (see page 118). The Dressage Skill also allows you to undertake the Dressage Activity between two adventures (see page 197). In combat, a successful opposed Taming/Mental Strength test allows you to intimidate a single animal belonging to your Specialization; you instill fear in the target animal until the end of your next turn (see page 190). When you instill fear in this way, you can subsequently use your Taming Skill instead of Close Combat when defending against your target; with the GM’s approval, you can also use Tame to attack your target, giving specific instructions. - Example: Confronting a hungry war dog, Ilse passes an opposed Dog Training Test in the first Combat Round, scaring the beast and gaining +1 Advantage. During the following Round, she “attacks“ her target with her Training Skill, bypassing the dog’s defense. Her GM allows her to command the beast to flee, which she does with her tail between her legs."

"This refers to your ability to climb on smooth or vertical surfaces. If time is not an issue, and climbing is relatively easy, anyone with the Climbing Skill is automatically considered capable of climbing any reasonable small height. In all other cases, please refer to page 165, which also covers Escalation during combat. You may even find yourself climbing tall obstacles, although in this case the notion of caution remains debatable."

"This Skill lets you pick pockets, retract objects, and perform small conjuring tricks, as well as cheat at games of chance. This Skill is generally opposed to your target’s Perception Skill; a Success means you’ve taken the item, picked pockets, or swapped cards, while a Minimal Success may suggest that your poor moves have made your opponent wary. You can also use Escamotage to “help“ your Betting Skill when playing an appropriate game of chance. Before each Round (or equivalent, depending on the game in question), you can attempt an Escamotage Test (which will be opposed if others are suspicious). On a success, you may reverse your Betting Test for the Round if it results in a success. Escamotage and combat rarely mix, although inventive Players may be able to create a spectacular diversion with the GM’s approval, perhaps even gaining an Advantage by making a dagger appear out of nowhere, surprising a superstitious enemy. "

"Dodging is your ability to avoid objects, by dodging, diving or moving quickly. It is often used to avoid falling rocks, blows, unexpected traps and so on. In combat, dodging is generally used to resist attacks or avoid damage. See Chapter 5: Rules for more information."

"Valuation lets you determine the value of rare artifacts, unusual merchandise and works of art. Everyone is supposed to know the relative value of ordinary objects, but successful use of Valuation allows you to determine the value of strange and specific objects. A successful Appraisal Test can also tell you whether the goods (or parts) you are analyzing are counterfeit - this Test is usually opposed to the DR of the Counterfeiter’s Art or Craft Test. Your GM can apply modifiers based on the rarity or unfamiliarity of the item, or on your Character’s specific Skills or background."

"The Focusing Skill measures your ability to call upon and control the various Winds of Magic. It is only used in conjunction with the magic rules. See Chapter 8: Magic for more information. Focusing is a very special Skill, in that it is both Grouped, enabling Specializations, but also non-Grouped for those not properly trained in focusing magic."

"This Skill means you are trained to heal wounds and diseases. A successful Heal Test allows you to do one of the following: Diagnose a pathology, infection, or disease. Treat a disease (see page 186) Heal a number of Wound Points equal to your Intelligence Bonus + DR (Note: a patient can only benefit from one Healing roll after each encounter). If sterile fluids or appropriate dressings and poultices are used, no Infection will develop from the injury (see page 181). Stop a Bleeding State (each DR removes an additional Bleeding State). A failed Healing Test can potentially cause Wounds if your total Intelligence Bonus + DR is less than 0. On an Amazing Failure, your patient will also contract a Minor Infection (see page 187). If you are caring for a sick person, a successful Heal Test protects you from sickness for that day. Each DR also prevents another Character who encounters the patient that same day from contracting the disease. For each full day the patient remains in your care, the duration of illness is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 1. For more information, see Illness and Infection in Chapter 5: Rules. . Some injuries require surgery; see the Surgery Talent for details. For more information on how to heal wounds, refer to Chapter 5: Rules. Your GM may apply modifiers to Cure Tests to illustrate the virulence of the disease, the suitability of conditions and materials, or the stress of your situation. If you heal someone during a fight, the Tests will most likely be Intermediate (+0)."

"This Skill allows you to coerce or scare conscious creatures. The precise way to initiate a Bullying Test depends on the context: although it is usually accompanied by an unconcealed threat, it can sometimes be a subtle hint or even a glance. Bullying is almost always opposed to the Quiet Skill of your target; on a success, you can bully a number of targets equal to your Force Bonus + DR. Each target will react to the Intimidation based on their own personality and how you managed to threaten them, but in any case they will step back or stray from the path and will not report you, or they will consider fighting the only solution and prepare their weapons. In combat, you provoke fear (see page 190) in all Intimidated targets. You can also use your Intimidation Skill instead of Body to Body when you defend yourself against those who are afraid of you, forcing the intimidated to leave the fight by your will and your only posture. Also, with your GM’s approval, you can use Intimidation to “attack” such targets, dictating specific orders, such as “drop your weapon” or “get out of there.” However, if you fail one of these Subsequent Intimidation Tests, you no longer intimidate (or cause fear) the opponents affected. With the approval of your GM, you can try to Intimidate them again in a future Round, but this leads to a negative modifier, since having already seen your bluster, they are less likely to fear you - Example: Facing a group of wooly drawers, Svetlana the Powerful gets 4 DRs in her Intimidation Test. Combined with its BF of 5, this means that it can affect up to 9 targets, more than enough to affect the three wooly drawers that are now Afraid of Svetlana. As she won by 3 DRs, she also wins +1 Advantage until the end of her next round. In the next round, she “attacks” the wooly pullers using her Intimidation, intending to scare them until they leave her alone. However, she fails the Test, and the wooldrawers realize that they are more numerous than her, and armed... - OPTION: ALTERNATIVE CHARACTERISTICS FOR INTIMIDATION. Although Force is the default statistic for Bullying Tests, DOJ may find situations that allow you to use a different trait: a relentless Redeemer can, for example, use Mental Force to deter a prying passerby, or an academic can use Intelligence to intimidate an ordinary student with his or her impressive knowledge."

"Intuition Skill lets you perceive what’s around you, notice when something is wrong, and feel when people are hiding something from you. Successful use of Intuition Skill gives you subtle and implicit information about your environment, as determined by your DOJ. It can be information, such as whether someone believes what he says, the general attitude toward the local noble, or whether the helpful local people’s intentions are as pure as they seem. If someone actively tries to conceal their intentions, they can resist your Intuition with Calm or Entertainment (Interpretation). In combat, a successful Intuition Test can be used to give you +1 Advantage as you evaluate the environment and your opponents. You can continue to strengthen your Advantage in subsequent rounds provided you are able to observe your targets and are not interrupted (for example, by being attacked); in this way you can gain a maximum of Advantages equal to your Intelligence Bonus."

"Language Proficiency indicates your fluency with different languages. All Characters are considered able to speak “reikspiel” - the language of the Empire - and their mother tongue (if your Character has a different language from reikspiel), without the need to do a Test. If your game is not in the Empire, replace Reikspiel with the local language. If you have any of these skills, you are usually able to make yourself understood in that language, or to understand simple concepts. You will be asked to do a Language Proficiency Test when a particularly difficult concept needs to be transmitted, or when an obscure dialect or vocabulary is used. Note: Language (Magick) is used to cast Spells and may, from time to time, require a Test with... unfortunate consequences if it fails. Refer to Chapter 8: Magic for more information. . - OPTION: LANGUAGE (BATTLE). The Language (Battle) comprises a series of simple commands and gestures that can be used in the heat of battle. A Character possessing Language (Battle) can communicate briefly with another Character during a fight, and without penalty. Those without the Skill cannot quickly coordinate their attacks or discuss strategy once combat has begun. - OLD WORLD LANGUAGES. Here is a list of the main languages of the Old World, as well as the people who speak them most commonly. There are a considerable number of other languages spoken, but they are far less often encountered in Reikland. Albionese: the people of Albion, who hail from the remote, foggy island kingdom and are rarely met. Battle: Old World warriors. Widespread among soldiers and mercenaries, it is used to give quick orders during battle. It was supposedly developed by the goddess Myrmidia when she surveyed the Old World as a mortal. Bretonnien: the people of Bretonnie, often met in Reikland. Bretonnie is a chivalrous kingdom in the southwest of the Empire. Classical: human academics of all kinds. It is the first known human language of the Old World - more than 3,000 years old - used in most scholarly texts of the Empire, including in the wizards’ scriptures and many sacred books. Elthárin: the people of Athel Loren, Lorenlorn and the passing merchants from Ulthuan. Elthárin is the language of the elves. The language has many ancient dialects, and is reputed to be very difficult for non-Elves to learn. Estalian: The people of Estonia, from the warm kingdoms of the South-West, known for their strong politics and their worship of the goddess Myrmidia. Gospodarin: The robust Kislev people, from the frozen oblast in the eastern part of the Empire. The language is often called “Kislevarin” or “Kislevarin” by foreigners. Grumbarth: ogres; few other people learn the language, although some mercenary commanders find it convenient for communicating with ogres they can hire. Khazalid: The people of Karaz Ankor, the dwarf kingdom in the mountains. The language is also widely spoken in the Sigmar Worship, which worships the strong relationship Sigmar had with the dwarves when he was mortal. Magick: the Wizards; this language sculpts the Winds of Magic into physical effects. The university form of the language taught by the Colleges of Magic is called Lingua Praestantia, far removed from the degraded form of the language used by witches and the uninitiated. It’s not used to communicate. Halfling: the people of the Moot; the great Halfling province of the Empire. This language is little known outside the word. Norse: the people of Norsca. Norse is commonly spoken in the northern part of the Empire in Nordland and Ostland, and is also widely known in Wasteland and Kislev. Reikspiel: the people of the Empire. Reikspiel is the main language used. It is expressed in innumerable distinct dialects throughout the Empire, many of which are mutually intelligible. This is the modern version of the language spoken by the God-King Sigmar when he was still mortal more than 2,500 years ago. Queekique: the people of the Sub-Empire. Used by the skavens and their many slaves. Few admit to speaking it, or even knowing it exists. Tilean: the people of Tileus, who are mainly found in the Empire as traders or mercenaries. The principalities of Tileia, in the south, are known for their relentless politics and their reverence for Myrmidia. The language of thieves: the people of the streets of the Old World. The expressions of this language are very localized and specific to each kingdom; for example"

"Bargaining allows you to get better deals when negotiating with others. In general, Bargaining is used to find out whether or not you are making a good deal, most of the time thanks to an Opposite Bargaining Test. More specifically, this Skill can be used when you browse the shops to find the best prices. For more information, see Chapter 11: Equipment Guide."

"Many people in Reikland embrace a profession; even adventurers often have a more reliable or respectable career to rely on between thrilling episodes. Business Proficiency represents your ability to create something or provide a service, as well as your knowledge of the essential knowledge surrounding your profession. Having the Skill is enough to automatically perform the tasks associated with your profession, assuming you have the right resources and tools. You only need to perform a Trade Test if you are looking to create something quickly, if conditions are unfavorable, or if you are looking to invent or create a high-quality object. Trades Tests of this type are often Extensive Tests, the DR. and the time required depend on the scope or scale of what is produced; a quick meal with Métier (Cook) to impress a local lord will take much less time than building a warship with Métier (Marine Carpenter). You can also perform a Trade Test as an Insight Skill to determine important information about the profession in question. In such circumstances, the DOJ may prefer to use the Int rather than the Dex as the Basic Feature, although this is often ignored to simplify. Although many Trade Skills are of little use in combat, there are as many Trade Skills as there are occupations, and some may be used depending on the circumstances. For example, passing a Trade Test (Apothecary) can be useful if you are fighting in an Apothecary stall because you identify bitter substances to throw at your enemies. Skill is also used to carry out a Craft Activity (see page 196)."

"It’s about your ability to play a musical instrument, good enough, we hope, to impress others. A successful Music Test allows you to entertain people close enough to see and hear you; the DR. indicates the quality of the song played."

"It’s your ability to swim in water without drowning. If you have the Swimming Skill, you are automatically able to swim freely without performing a Test. But if you find yourself in rough currents, in hot pursuit, or fleeing a giant shark sent by Stromfels, the god of Drowning, a Test will be necessary. It can be altered by water conditions, or the bulk of your clothing, armor, or other gear. Swimming is used in combat, only if you happen to fight in water. So it replaces Skills such as Athletics to determine Movement. If a set speed is needed, you swim at half your Move Characteristic, using the normal rules for moving found on page 164."

"Orientation allows you to find your way in nature using landmarks, stellar bodies or maps. Possessing the Orientation Skill means that you know roughly where you are, and can determine your path by well-known landmarks without making a Test. A Test is only necessary if you are disoriented or traveling off the beaten track. A success then points you in the right direction or allows you to avoid mishaps. If you are on a long journey, your GM may ask you to perform an extended Orientation Test, modified by weather conditions, visible landmarks, and access to reliable geographic information. The DR needed to pass depends on how far the destination is, and each Test represents between an hour and a day of travel, depending on the nature of the journey."

"This Skill allows you to evaluate the probability that a bet will pay off, and to successfully participate in different games of chance. When placing a bet, all Players perform a Betting Test – applying any appropriate modifiers for their knowledge of the game – and the Player with the highest DR wins. In the event of a tie, all Players with the lowest scores retire, and the remaining Players take another Test Bet, repeating this process until one Player wins. If you want to influence the game in less honest ways, see Sneaking. - OPTION. Some Players prefer to use immersive mini-games at the table, playing real card or dice games for easier interpretation. If you opt for this solution, a successful Gamble Test will allow you to influence the game – by drawing, for example, an additional card or by re-rolling a die – as decided by the GM. Each DR grants you an additional opportunity to influence the game."

"From simple snares, or wolftraps, to the most spectacular devices such as Von Grizzel’s Coating-Thief, Players are unlikely to venture far into the Old World without encountering traps. The Trap Skill measures your ability to set and disarm traps of all kinds. Anyone who possesses it is automatically considered capable of activating and disarming traps given enough time. A Test is usually only necessary if you are trying to use the Skill quickly or under pressure, or if the trap is particularly complex. A sample of simple traps can be found in Chapter 11: Equipment Guide. Setting or disarming most traps requires an Accessible (+20%) Trap Test, but more complex devices may require an extended Test, requiring multiple DRs over several Rounds."

"You are able to follow subtle tracks left by others. Tracking is used to follow difficult tracks in nature. This is not a Skill to track down a set of footprints in the snow, as a simple Perception Test is sufficient for this. Tracking involves deeper knowledge and awareness to recognize the subtle signs of passing prey. You can also attempt to cover your tracks, in which case your Tracking Skill is opposed to your pursuer’s Tracking Test. An extended Tracking Test is often necessary to follow a track, the Difficulty of which is modified by the freshness of the tracks, and by the state of the ground: damp earth betrays the passage better than stony ground. The GM can also use the Pursuit rules to determine if you are successful in tracking down fleeing prey (see page 166)."

"This is your ability to perceive things with your senses – sight, smell, hearing, touch and taste, and any other senses such as magical or non-human senses. Your GM may ask you to make a Perception Test to detect something, such as movement behind the tree line, the presence of a trap, or someone following you, modified by the ease of noticing it. Perception is also used to resist attempts to conceal things through Skills such as Concealment or Stealth. Perception has many uses in combat, most often for noticing important details beyond what is evident in the surrounding environment and your opponents, as determined by the GM."

"This is your ability to summon or commune with a deity. For more information on using the Prayer Skill in hopes of divine intervention, see Chapter 7: Religions and Beliefs. In combat, if your GM deems it appropriate given your situation and your faith, you can use Prayer to meditate and concentrate. Each Round you spend praying in combat – passing a Prayer Test – you gain +1 Advantage. This way, you can earn additional Perks, up to a maximum equal to your Fellowship Bonus. Additionally, if your enemies understand your language and know (or fear) your deity, the GM may allow you to use Prayer instead of the Intimidate Skill."

"Although anyone can throw a simple rock using the Shot Skill, it takes training and practice to use weapons like bows and pistols. Each Projectile Specialization represents a particular group of ranged weapons. If you do not have the Missiles Specialization for a weapon you wish to use, refer to Chapter 11: Equipment Guide to see what penalties you will incur when using it. See Chapter 5: Rules for more details on ranged combat."

"This Skill allows you to quickly unearth useful and interesting information, and spread your own rumors. A successful Gossip Test means you have found some useful information, which your GM can pass on to you, about the region. Each DR gives you either additional information or the chance to spread a rumor to a number of people equal to your Sociability Bonus. The time needed for a Gossip Test depends on how cautious the Players are, and how populated the area is, which is decided by the GM. It’s unlikely that Ragot could be useful in combat, but if your attacker happens to be local and you know something really juicy… - WHISPER. While sharing information gleaned from Gossip Tests with all Players at once may be convenient for the GM, it is also often more pleasant to only share information individually, Player by Player (by a note or by talking quickly with them aside). This means that Players must link information together – promoting immersion and interpretation – which can lead to errors and misunderstandings, sometimes leading to hilarious, or horrifying results."

"This is your skill at paddling and steering a boat through water. The Rowing Skill is typically used in chases, to cross rapids, desperately avoid bog octopuses, or for similar unusual or dangerous feats. Anyone with the Skill is automatically considered able to glide skillfully across a calm pond or river without a Test. Those without the Skill may have to make a Test, except for basic maneuvers."

"It is about your ability to unearth useful and often obscure knowledge from libraries and other repositories of information. Research requires the Read/Write Talent (see page 140). Simply having the Search Skill indicates that you can find simple information in a clearly indexed library without Testing given enough time. If you are looking for specific less well-known information, or if you are in a hurry, you will need to perform an Extended Search Test, the Difficulty of which is modified by the size of the library, and the target DR depends on the obscurity of the subject. Seek has no use in combat, except perhaps to unearth a useful manual on sword fighting techniques. - RESEARCH AND LIBRARY. Old World libraries range from small personal units comprising a few dozen books to extensive archives in universities and temples in towns and cities. Performing a Search Test in a small library, perhaps to find a particular book, will only take about 5 minutes. By comparison, Research Tests in large libraries can easily take an hour or more per Test, but are more likely to lead to the discovery of arcane knowledge."

"You learned a physically demanding art, probably for a living, perhaps as an acrobat or a member of a traveling carnival. Successful use of the Perform Skill allows you to entertain all spectators close enough to see and hear you; the DR indicates how successful you have been. Some Perform physical specializations can give you Advantage in combat. With your GM’s approval, Perform (Acrobatics) can be used instead of Dodge. Other Perform Skills can be used directly as a weapon if you have the appropriate equipment, such as Perform (Fire Breather)!"

"This is your ability to consume alcohol without it clouding your judgment or making you unreasonable. After each alcoholic drink, take an Alcohol Resistance Test, modified by the strength of the drink. For each Test you fail, you suffer a -10 penalty to your CC, CT, Ag, Dex and Int, up to a maximum of -30 per Attribute. If you fail a number of Tests equal to your Endurance Bonus, you are Drunk. Roll on the following table to see the consequences: 1–2: “Valour of the Marienburgher! » : Gain a +20 bonus to your Calm Skill. 3–4: “You are my best friend!“ » : Ignore all your existing Prejudices and Animosities (see page 190). 5–6: “Why is the room spinning? » : On your turn, you can either perform a Movement or an Action, but not both (see page 157). 7–8: “I’ll take you all one by one!“ » : Gain Animosity (Everyone!) (see page 190). 9–10 “How did I get here?“ » : You wake up the next day with a terrible hangover and few memories of what happened. The GM and other Players who were with you will fill in the awkward gaps if you seek to find out. Pass an Alcohol Resistance Test or gain a Poisoned State (see page 168). After an hour without drinking, perform an Intermediate (+0) Alcohol Resistance Test. The effects of drunkenness wear off after 10-DR hours, and all Trait modifiers wear off after that time. Once all effects have dissipated, perform a new Intermediate (+0) Alcohol Resistance Test. You now have the Hangover, which is the Exhausted State and cannot be removed for 5 – DR hours. You can spend 1 Point of Resolve to ignore negative drunk modifiers until the end of the next Round (see page 171)."

"The Resistance Skill is called upon when you have to endure harsh conditions, face deprivation, wait motionless for a long period of time, or survive in hostile environments. More specifically, Resistance Tests are used to resist or recover from different States (see page 167) and help you recover your lost Wound Points. Refer to Chapter 5: Rules for more information on this."

"Possing a Knowledge Skill means that you have formally studied, or learned in some way, a branch of advanced knowledge. You have in-depth data in a specialization and therefore do not need to take a Test for the GM to give you the useful information. If you are looking for specific lesser-known information, you will need to perform a Knowledge Test, modified according to the obscure nature of the information, where the DRs will indicate how many details you remember. In combat, a successful Knowledge Test may eventually grant you +1 Advantage (with your GM’s approval). For example, Knowledge (Geology) can give you an Advantage if you are fighting in a cave, or Knowledge (Engineering) can help you if you are fighting an enemy armed with a complex mechanical device. You may continue to build your Advantage in later turns, provided circumstances permit (determined by GM) and you are not interrupted; this way, you can gain a maximum of Advantages, equal to your Intelligence Bonus."

"You have been trained to use covert marks intelligible to members of a selected group. The reasons why someone may want to deliver a secret message are many: wanderers may want to indicate which owners are likely to offer charity, thieves may want to indicate loopholes, or potential targets, while lookouts may want to alert the others on the location near a dangerous monster. This Skill does not usually require a Test - you can decipher any appropriate signs you can see if you have this Skill. But if the signs have been altered, erased, or you’re pressed for time, a Test will likely be required. Most messages are very simple, with no more than three words. - I SAW THE SIGN. Here is a list of the main secret signs of the Old World, and who uses them. This is just a small sample of the most commonly used in Reikland, and this list is far from exhaustive. We encourage you to create the ones that best suit your game. Gray Order: The mysterious Gray Wizards use a complex set of signs, many of which are only noticeable to wizards. They mark the region for their wandering Magisters, indicating safe houses, dangerous places, regions where they are not welcome, and much more. Guild: guilds. Many large guilds, from masons to stevedores, use a set of marks and signs to identify what is important to their members. Rural: people of the woods and other country peoples. Pathfinder signs are most often used to mark territory, to point out an important or dangerous area, and to mark safe paths. Lookout: Scouts, especially those Hired by military and mercenary companies. Signs are most often used to point out supply areas, routes for food convoys, and notable hazards uphill. Thief: Thieves and rogues. The various gangs and criminal organizations in towns and cities use a multitude of marks to indicate safe havens, soft targets, frequently patrolled areas, etc. Vagabond: vagabonds and peddlers. Vagrant signs are most often used to identify safe places to sleep, villages to avoid, and sources of food and water."

"Animal Care Skill allows you to care for animals and heal them when they get sick or injured. Having a single Animal Care Increase means you can keep animals healthy without having to check. You can also perform an Animal Care Test to identify and solve problems with animals such as: Detecting disease. Understand the reasons for disobedience or discomfort. Determine the specifics of the animal. Heal a number of wounds equal to the Intelligence Bonus + DR (Note: an animal can only benefit from one Healing roll after each encounter) Stop a Bleeding State. Prepare the animal for a demonstration. In combat, you can assess an enemy animal with an Animal Care Test. On a success, you, and anyone you notify, gain +10 to hit when attacking that animal – or anyone using it as a mount – until the end of your next turn, as you notice a loose harness, lameness caused by a minor injury, or highlight any other weakness or vulnerability. Heal Animals can only provide a maximum of +10 to hit per animal, regardless of the number of Tests taken to detect a weakness. - ANIMALS. It’s up to the GM to decide whether Animal Care and Taming work with a creature or not. While for some – dog, horse, half-griffon – the answer seems obvious, for others it is much less so. You can debate whether or not a dragon could benefit from Taming, but try explaining that to the dragon in question..."

"This is your ability to judge whether or not someone is likely to accept a bribe, and how best to present it to them so that they accept it. A successful Bribery Test tells you if a target can be bribed. If so, your GM secretly determines the price of his cooperation using the target’s Income (see page 52), increasing the amount according to his usual honesty and the risk involved in accepting the bribe. Then you estimate that target amount and the GM will let you know if the price is higher, lower, or equal. Each DR obtained during your Bribery Test gives you an additional estimate. At the end of this process, you determine how much money to offer, based on the information obtained. - Example: Snorri tries to bribe a Guard to let him pass; he is a Bronze 2 Character, which means he has an Income of 4d10 copper coins. The GM decides the guard can be bribed and secretly rolls 21 on the 4d10, indicating that the price to bribe the guard is 21 copper cents. Letting Snorri pass isn’t too risky for the Guard, he does it often, so the GM doesn’t increase the necessary bribe. Snorri rolled 1 DR on his Bribery Test; he therefore knows that the Guard is receptive to the bribe, and has 2 guesses to find the price. Snorri’s first estimate is 15 copper cents, to which his GM replies “Superior“. His second estimate is 40, to which his GM responds, “Inferior.“ Snorri now knows he has to pay the guard a bribe of between 15 and 40 copper cents. He decides to aim high and offers 30 copper cents. With a smile on his face, the Guard leads Snorri across. In combat, you can use Bribery like this to try to stop the fight, but consider the Test Hard (-20) due to the stress of the situation. If your target isn’t receptive, you can’t offer a bribe, or if your target doesn’t speak your language, your pathetic attempts to bribe them will be futile. Obviously, if they have the advantage of numbers, what could possibly stop them from taking all your money?"

"The Outdoor Survival Skill is used for survival in the wild, and includes the ability to fish, hunt, forage, make a fire, and build shelter. Experienced travelers are good at spotting signs of changing weather and the droppings of many dangerous beasts. When camping, make a Survival Test outdoors, modified by the harshness of the conditions – for example, a Test is Intermediate (+0) if it rains, Hard (-20) in a storm. A successful Test indicates that you can obtain food and shelter for the night. Each DR allows you to obtain the equivalent for one more Character. If the Test fails, you must make an Intermediate (+0) Resistance Test or receive the Exhausted State. If you suffer an Amazing Failure, something untoward has happened, as determined by the GM; perhaps your camp is attacked during the night? When fighting in the wilderness, you can make a Survival Test outdoors to gain +1 Advantage, similar to Intuition, for a maximum number of Advantages equal to your Intelligence Bonus, because you spot dangerous or interesting terrain to use to your advantage. - OPTION: FIND FOOD AND HERBS. Finding food and herbs normally takes about 2 hours. Hunting and foraging parties perform a Sustained Outdoor Survival Test for the group, the Difficulty of which is determined by the circumstances. Food Search: A success provides enough food for a Character. Each DR provides enough food for one more person. Hunt and Fish: If you have the appropriate bows, spears, fishing rods or nets, a successful Test allows you to feed two people, and two additional people per DR. Trap: Use the Trap Skill to place animal traps (see page 304). Can feed the same number of people as Hunt and Fish. Lore (Herbs): If you prefer to gather herbs using Lore (Herbs), a success allows you to gather a dose of the sought-after herb (see page 307), and each DR adds an additional dose. Foraging Tests are modified based on Herb Availability: Common (0), Limited (-10), Rare (-20), or Exotic (-30)."

"This is your ability to steer and maneuver a sailboat – including managing knots, rudder, wind measurement, etc. Assuming you have a well-trained crew on your ship, you only use the Sail Skill when you need to push your ship for a chase, to navigate particularly dangerous shoals, to fight against bad conditions weather, or during similar difficulties. Merely sailing in calm winds or guiding a boat in the direction of the current does not require a Test for those who have Sail. The Skill can also be used for sailing-related activities, such as tying knots or using them to tie people up. As all sailboats are pretty much the same to steer, owning one Specialization makes the others Basic for you."

Talent.Explanation: "RANDOM TALENTS."

"You are capable of incredible feats on horseback. You can use any of your Unmodified Perform and Dodge Skills while mounted. Additionally, when mounted, you may perform your Move at the start of the Round instead of your Turn."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Fellowship Stat (which does not count as Raises)."

"Wild animals feel confident in your presence, and tend to follow you. All creatures with the Bestial Trait not trained to be aggressive will automatically be calm in your presence, unless they have a reason not to be, such as pain, an attack, natural hyper-aggressiveness, or a young. near."

"You can use your non-leading hand much better than most people, through training or innate talent. You only suffer a -10 penalty to Tests relying solely on your off-hand instead of -20. If you have this Talent twice, you suffer no penalty."

"Your soul is pure, very resistant to the depredations of Chaos. You may gain an additional number of Corruption Points equal to your Pure Soul level before you have to take a Test to see if you are Corrupted."
"You can easily reload Black Powder weapons. Add a DR equal to your Gunner level to any Extended Test to reload a Black Powder weapon."

"You have a natural talent for art, and can produce accurate drawings with a little time and the right medium. This ability has several in-game uses, ranging from creating wanted posters to illustrating specialized journals, and has specific Advantages determined by the GM. Also add Art (Any) to any Career you start; if it is already included in the Career, you can instead buy the Skill for 5 XP less per Increase."

"Your blows follow each other in rapid succession, raining down on your opponents with the fury of Ulric. Once per Round, if you hit an opponent in close combat, you can immediately expend an Advantage or your Movement to perform an additional attack (assuming you have your Movement remaining)."

"Whether it’s your piercing gaze, your muscular body, or perhaps the sparkle of your perfect teeth, you know how to best use what the gods have given you. When you successfully use Charm to influence those who find you Attractive, you can choose to use either the DR of your roll or the number of units rolled on your die. Therefore, a hit of 63 can be used as a +3 DR."
Talent.Test: "Charm test to influence those who find you attractive."

Talent.Explanation: "Called ’talking wildly’ in Nordland, or simply ’talking nonsense’ in Ostland, Chattering consists of speaking quickly incessantly, or speaking long and voluble, talking about unimportant or unimportant things. meaningless, to verbally confuse and confuse a target. You use your Charm Skill to Chat. Attempt an opposed Charm/Intelligence Test. A success gives your opponent a Stunned State. Additionally, for each level you have in this Talent, your opponent gains an additional Stunned State. Targets Stunned by Chatter can do nothing but stare at you, dumbfounded and trying to follow or understand what you are saying. Once the last Stunned State comes to an end, the target can finally place a word, and may not be very happy with you. After all, you’ve been talking about unimportant or meaningless things for quite a long time. If you stop talking, your opponent immediately loses any Stunned States caused by your Chatter Talent. In general, you can only attempt to Tweak a Character once per scene, or longer (the GM determines this point), because the target soon becomes aware of your antics."

"You are trained to deliver precise, controlled strikes to your opponent’s weapon, creating an opening for an attack or simply preventing an attack from reaching you. For your Action, you can choose Beat before rolling the dice. Perform a Close Combat Test; on a success, your opponent loses -1 Advantage and -1 more per DR you rolled. This Test is not opposed. This Talent is useless if your opponent does not carry a weapon, or is of a Size greater than yours (see page 342)."

"You are protected by one of the gods and you can intensify the power of simple Prayers. You can now use the Blessings of your deity listed in Chapter 7: Religions and Beliefs. Under normal conditions, you can only know one Divine Lore for the Blessed Talent."

"You are experienced in traversing difficult terrain. You ignore all Movement penalties when crossing specific terrain. Common specializations include: Coastline, Deserts, Swamps, Rocky, Tundra, Woodlands."
"You have strong legs capable of carrying you great distances when you jump. Add your Good Legs level to your DR on all Athletics Tests involving Jumping (see page 166)."
"You’re kind of a jack-of-all-trades, capable of fixing almost anything. You treat all nonmagical Job Skills as Basic when repairing broken items."

"You are used to making do with little, and know how to survive lean times. You can subsist on half the food you need without negative penalties (preventing you from actually being hungry), and you only need to make a Hunger Test every 3 days, not 2 (see page 181)."
"You managed to maintain a respectable appearance despite your misdeeds. You can ignore Status lost due to Criminal Talent."

"You are comfortable in the saddle even in the most difficult situations, and know how to get the best out of your mount during conflict. Assuming you have the Ride Skill, you can directly command your mount to perform an Action, not just a Move, without a Ride Test."
"They say that when you were born, Ranald smiled. Your maximum Luck Points are now equal to your current number of Fate Points, plus the number of times you got Lucky."

"You rush at your enemies with boundless recklessness, using the force of your charge to add weight to your strikes. When performing a Berserk Charge, you inflict +1 point of Damage per level in this Talent to all Melee attacks."
Talent.Test: "Melee on a Round when performing a Berserk Charge"

Talent.Explanation: "You are at home in dark alleys. When using Stealth (Urban), you may reverse the roll of any failed Test if it results in a Success."

"You are a surgeon, able to open and close flesh to heal. You can treat any Critical Injury requiring Surgery. You can also perform Surgery to solve internal problems with an extended Intermediate (+0) Healing Test whose target DR is determined by the GM (usually 5-10) depending on the difficulty of the procedure in progress. This causes 1d10 Wounds and 1 Bleeding State per Test, which means the Surgery has a high chance of killing the patient if the practitioner is not careful. After the Surgery, the patient must pass an Accessible (+20) Resistance Test or gain a Minor Infection (see page 187)."
Talent.Test: "Healing Tests outside of Combat Rounds; when you have time to do it right."

Talent.Explanation: "You know how to get the most out of your animals. When an animal you control Flees or Runs, it gains +1 Movement if you use a whip."
Talent.Test: "Hitch or Ride Tests while Fleeing or Running."

Talent.Explanation: "No matter how bad things get, you still persevere. You can attempt a Calm Test to remove a Broken State at the end of each of your Turns as well as at the end of the Round (see page 168 for details)."

"You have learned all the dirty tricks of unarmed combat. You can choose to inflict +1 additional Damage for each level of Unfair Combat, for all successful hits with Close Combat (Brawl). Note: Using this Talent will be considered cheating in any official fight."

"You have learned to make the most of confined space combat. You ignore Close Combat penalties caused by confined spaces, such as tunnels, front lines, small pits, and similar places, and you can use the Dodge Skill, even if it is normally impossible due to the lack of space."
"You react as quickly as lightning. Your Initiative is 10 higher when determining Combat Initiative for each level you have in this Talent."

"You are trained to stand very close to an opponent. You do not suffer any penalty for fighting an opponent with a longer weapon than yours. Additionally, if you use the Melee Combat optional rules (see page 297), gain a +10 bonus to hitting your opponent."
Talent.Test: "Melee when fighting in close contact or going into close contact"

Talent.Explanation: "You are good at making potions, potions, and concoctions. You can perform a Crafting Activity for free to use Knowledge (Apothecary) without needing a Workshop. Other Craft Activities follow the normal rules."

"You can bend your body into a myriad of seemingly abnormal positions. This allows you to slip into unlikely spaces and manipulate your body in incredible ways, granting you Boons granted by the GM, possibly with a successful Agility Test."
"You are better able to control your Frenzy in combat. You can end it with a successful Calm Test at the end of the Round."

"You know what to say and when to have the most impact on your superiors. When you successfully use a Social Skill to influence those with higher Status, you can choose to use either the DR or the Units number on the die. So a hit of 46 can be used as a +6 DR."
"You are muscular and used to carrying heavy loads. Increase Encumbrance Points by a number equal to your Strongman level x 2."

"You have been trained to fight side by side with other soldiers. If an enemy causes you to lose Boons while standing next to an active ally with the Shoulder to Shoulder Talent, you may retain 1 lost Boon for each time you took the Shoulder to Shoulder Talent ."
Talent.Test: "Melee when standing next to an ally with Elbow to Elbow"

Talent.Explanation: "You know how to hit hard! You deal your Power Blow level as Extra Damage with Melee weapons."

"You are an active criminal making money from illegal sources, and you are not always discreet about it. To calculate your income, whether it is when you Earn money or when you perform an Income Activity, refer to the following table (1:+2d10 copper coins, 2:+1d10 silver pistols, 3:+2d10 silver pistols, 4:+1 gold crown) Because of your obvious criminal nature, others consider you of lower Status, unless they also possess the Criminal Talent. In this case, Status is compared as normal – maybe you have gang tattoos, look sleazy, or just a little rough, the choice is yours. Because of this, local law enforcement is always suspicious and doubts your motives. The longer you take this Talent, the worse it gets, with the exact repercussions determined by the GM. Those who break the law without possessing the Criminal Talent earn much less money, but since it is not notorious, they therefore retain their Status. With the GM’s approval, you can remove levels from the Criminal Talent for the same amount of XP as they cost to buy them."

"You are able to disarm an opponent with a judicious flick of the wrist or a well-aimed strike with your hand. For an Action, you can attempt an opposed Melee/Melee Test. On a hit, your opponent loses a held weapon, which lands 1d10x30cm in a random direction (with additional effects determined by the GM). If you succeed by 2 DRs, you can determine how far the weapon is thrown instead of making a throw; if you win 4 DRs, you can also choose the direction in which the weapon is thrown; if you win by 6 or more DRs, you can pick up your opponent’s weapon if you have a free hand, catching it mid-air with panache. This Talent is useless if your opponent has no weapon, or if he is of a Size greater than yours (see page 342)."

"You can tell when magic resides in an artifact. You may attempt an Intuition Test for any magical artifact hit. On a success, you feel the item is magical; in addition, each DR also learns a specific special rule regarding the item, if it has any. In principle, you can only attempt this Test once per artifact hit."
"You launch attacks with fierce determination. Add your Determined Talent level to your Strength Bonus when you Charge."

"You instinctively understand the Magick language and are able to quickly articulate the most complex sentences without error. You do not suffer an Imperfect Casting if you roll a double on a successful Language (Magick) Test."

"You are good at following people unnoticed. You can use the Shadowing rules on page 121 without performing a Combined Test. Instead, you simply make a Perception or Stealth Test, whichever is greater."

"You are trained to perform simple moves to distract or surprise your opponent, distracting them from your true intent. You can use your Movement to Distract. This is resolved by an opposed Athletics/Calm Test. On a success, your opponent gains no Advantage until the end of the next Round."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Dexterity (does not count as Augments)."
"You have a gift for calculating and find the solution to most mathematical problems easily. You can use a simple calculator to simulate what your PC can mentally count."
"You gain as many additional Wound Points as your Endurance Bonus. If the latter increases, the number of Wound Points conferred by Badass also increases."

"You are adept at breaking down doors quickly and carrying out break-ins. You can add +1 Damage for each level in this Talent when determining Damage to inanimate objects, such as windows, chests, doors, and similar objects."
Talent.Test: "Melee when forcing or breaking inanimate objects"

Talent.Explanation: "Any sane person thinks twice before approaching you. If you wish, you have a Fear Rating of 1 (see page 190). Add +1 to this Index per additional number of times you have taken this Talent."
"It takes a lot to finish you off. You may ignore the Wound Point lost due to Bleeding. Each level in this Talent allows you to ignore the Wound Point lost due to an additional Bleeding State."

"You are used to asserting your opinions and imposing them. If you pass a Charm Test to argue with an opponent, you can choose to either use the DR of your roll or the number of units rolled on your die. So a successful roll of 24 can be used as a +4 DR."

"You are good at embezzling money from your employers without getting caught. Each time you earn money (during the game or by performing an Income Activity), you may attempt an opposed Intelligence Test with your employer (assuming you have one). If you win, you embezzle 2d10+DR copper coins, 1d10+DR silver pistols, or 1+DR gold crowns (depending on the size of the transaction in question, as determined by the GM) without getting caught. . If your employer earns +6 DR, you earn your money, but your Scam is spotted; what happens next is up to the GM. Any other result means you failed to scam money."

"Your uplifting calls can turn the tide of battle. Refer to the following table to see how many people you can now influence with your Leadership Skill (see page 120) during a war. Number of soldiers influenced 1:Normal x 5.2:Normal x 10.3:Normal x 20.4:Normal x 50.5:Normal x 100.6:Normal x 200.7:Normal x 500.8:Normal x 1000.9:Anyone who can hear your inspirational voice"
"You are an experienced beggar, capable of winning over even the most cynical individuals. You can make a Charm Test every half hour while Begging, not every hour (see page 119)."

"You have learned how to make false attacks in close combat to fool your opponent. You can now fake your Action against any opponent using a weapon. This is resolved with an opposed Hand to Hand (Fencing)/Hand to Hand Test. If you win and attack the same opponent before the end of the next Round, you can add the DR of your Feint to the result of your roll."

"When you speak in defense of your cause, your situation, or your religion, your words vibrate with passion and burning fervour. You can double your Fellowship to calculate the number of people you influence with your Orator Talent (see page 142) when you advocate for your cause."
Talent.Test: "Charm when speaking up for your cause"

Talent.Explanation: "You have dedicated your pain to the service of your God. Each day, you must spend half a bell (half an hour) in prayer while continuing to inflict a number of Wounds on yourself equal to your Lasher Level. Until your next rest, if you have the Frenzy Talent, you can go into Frenzy immediately without making a Test. The Frenzy Talent is added to the Talents list of any of your Careers. If you fail to flog yourself on a given day, or if you allow your bruised flesh to heal, you cannot expend any Resilience and Resolve until you flog again."
Talent.Test: "Any Test to resist the Powers of Ruin"

Talent.Explanation: "You are used to getting into bad situations, and preferably getting out of them. You can attempt an Intuition Test to identify those who seek to cause trouble or harm you, even if you are not normally entitled to it, due to Talents or a Spell for example. This Test will likely be opposed if the others are concealed, and the GM may prefer to perform this Test on your behalf so that you don’t know the outcome if you fail. If spotted disruptors engage in combat, you can ignore any Surprised States they would normally have inflicted."

"You know where to hit an opponent to take them down quickly. You ignore the penalty for designating a Location to strike to the Head when you use a Melee weapon with the Stunning Perk (see page 297). Additionally, you consider all improvised weapons to have the Knock Out perk."
Talent.Test: "Melee Tests when performing a Stunning Strike"

Talent.Explanation: "You are an expert at hitting your enemies in the most vulnerable places. You inflict your Wounding Strike level in additional Wounds when you cause a Critical Wound."

"You’re good at hitting your enemy exactly where you want them, whether it’s Ranged or Melee. You can modify your Location result up to +/-10 per number of times you have taken this Talent. So if you took this Talent twice and got Location 34, Right Arm, you can change it to 14, Left Arm, or 54, Body (see page 159)."

"Your quick reactions allowed you to take down many enemies before they even had time to draw. While Charged, you may attempt an Intermediate (+0) Initiative Test to immediately gain a Free Attack outside of the normal turn sequence. This attack is resolved with any weapon you hold in your main hand. You can make as many Reactive Strikes in a Round as you have Levels in that Talent, but can only attack each Charging individual once."
Talent.Test: "Initiative Tests for Anything Related to this Talent"

Talent.Explanation: "You can enter Frenzy as described on page 190."
"When your life is at stake, you are capable of running at an impressive speed. Your Movement Attribute counts as if it were increased by 1 when fleeing (see page 165)."
"You are good at inflaming crowds. You gain a DR bonus equal to your Greatspeaker levels on any Charm Test when you speak in public in front of a crowd."

"You are an exceptional climber. You can attempt to climb even on surfaces that seem too smooth, such as sheer fortifications, icy platforms, plastered walls, etc. and you ignore any penalties to Climb Tests resulting from the difficulty of the surface being climbed."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting CC Stat (does not count as Augments)."

"You know all the tricks for navigating dangerous rivers. You do not need Tests to cross treacherous bodies of water until the Difficulty is -10 or less – you automatically pass all easier Tests. Additionally, if you have the appropriate Knowledge (Region) Skill, you never need to make Tests to navigate dangerous waters – as you are considered to know the routes to take."

"You are consumed by hatred for something in the Old World, as described on page 190. Each time you take this Talent, you develop some hatred for a new group. Here are some examples of groups you can hate: Beastmen, Greenskins, Monsters, Outlaws, Sigmarites, Undead, Dissenting Sorcerers."
"Your Prayers exude the hatred you feel for your blasphemous enemies. You deal +1 Damage with Miracles for each level in this Talent."
"Your experience, Talent or training allows you to more safely manipulate the Winds of Magic. You do not suffer an Imperfect Casting if you roll a double on a successful Focus Test."

"You maintain a secret identity that allows you to appear richer, or perhaps poorer, than you currently are. With GM approval, choose a Quarry. As long as you are dressed appropriately, you may use the Social Status of the borrowed Quarry chosen, rather than your own, to modify the Social Tests. You can even ignore the Criminal Talent. However, maintaining this identity will require Entertainment (Interpretation) Tests when you encounter those who might detect your trickery. You can create a new Secret Identity for each Level you have in this Talent."
Talent.Test: "Entertainment Tests (Interpretation) to support your secret identities"

Talent.Explanation: "You have a good ear for accents and dialects and for reproducing them accurately. You can copy any accent you are exposed to for at least one day through an Initiative Test; this Test can be attempted once per day. Once successful, you can still imitate the accent, and the natives will believe you are one of their own."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting FM Stat (this does not count as Raises)."

"When your mind is on a target, no one can stop you from hitting it. If you use Advantages when you Disengage, you may keep a number of Advantages equal to your Ruthless Level. Additionally, you can use Advantages to Disengage even if you have fewer Advantages than your opponents."

"You are a jaded veteran who has survived more than one round of gunfire from Black Powder weapons. You need to make a Calm Test to resist a Broken State only if you are successfully wounded by a Black Powder weapon, and not just targeted (see page 297)."
Talent.Test: "Calm Tests to Resist Black Powder Panic"

Talent.Explanation: "You have a strong backbone, used to hard work. You may add your Indefatigable Levels to your DR in all opposed Strength Tests and you may carry a number of additional Encumbrance Points (see p293) equal to your Indefatigable Level."

"The great and powerful pay no heed to your presence, knowing that you are not worthy of notice. Assuming you are properly dressed and not in an incongruous position, people of a higher Status Rank will ignore you unless your presence is inappropriate, which can make it very easy to listen in on conversations you don’t. aren’t supposed to hear. Additionally, Characters of a higher Status Tier than you do not gain Advantage when defeating you in combat, as there is no merit in defeating such a poor wretch."
Talent.Test: " Discretion when you are in plain sight"

Talent.Explanation: "You are a master of politics and unearth conspiracies wherever they hide. Once per session, you may ask the GM a question regarding a political situation or complex social organization; the GM will perform a secret Intelligence Test and provide you with some observations on the situation based on your DR."
Talent.Test: "Intelligence Tests for everything related to this Talent"

Talent.Explanation: "You are blessed by one of the gods, and can therefore perform one of the Miracles of your cult. Additionally, you can purchase additional Miracles for 100 XP per Miracle you currently know. So if you already know 3 Miracles, your next Miracle will cost you 300 XP. The complete rules for learning new Miracles can be found in Chapter 7: Religions and Beliefs. Under normal conditions, you cannot learn more than one Summoning Talent (Divine Lore). Also, you cannot learn the Minor Magic or Arcane Magic Talents while you have the Summoning Talent. You can unlearn this Talent for 100 XP, but you will lose all of your Miracles if you do so, and you will incur extreme disfavor from your God, the effects of which are determined by the GM."

"You read the books at a frantic pace. You may reverse a failed Research Test if doing so makes it successful. If the speed at which you read is important during a fight, a successful Language Test allows you to read and understand a number of pages per Round equal to your DR plus your Speed Reading level (minimum 1, even if you have failed the Test)."
Talent.Test: "Search and Language if reading speed is important"

Talent.Explanation: "You have a natural affinity for languages. After a month of listening to any Language, you consider the associated Language Skill a Basic Skill through a successful Intelligence Test (which can be attempted once a month). Note: Linguistic Talent only works for languages used to communicate with others, so it does not work with Language (Magick)."

"You can understand what people are saying just by staring at their lips; you don’t need to hear what they say. If you have a clear view of the speaker’s lower face, you can attempt a Perception Test to figure out what they are saying."
Talent.Test: "Perception Tests for anything related to this Talent"

Talent.Explanation: "You are one of the few literate individuals in the Old World. You are considered to be able to read and write (if necessary) all the Languages you speak."

"You are an experienced sailor, and are fully accustomed to life at sea. You may ignore any negative modifiers to Sea Trials resulting from adverse weather, ship roll, and similar situations. Additionally, you count as two sailors towards the minimum number of crew needed to pilot an ocean-going vessel."
Talent.Test: " Sailing (any vessel capable of sailing at sea)"

Talent.Explanation: "You are of strong build and can withstand the strongest blows. Each time you gain one or more Stunned States, you can immediately make an Intermediate (+0) Resistance Test to ignore one, with each DR removing an additional Stunned State."

"You are trained to use magic in the midst of combat. On your Turn, you can cast a Spell with an Incantation Level of 5 or less for free, without using your Action. However, if you do, you cannot cast any other Spells this Turn."

"You know one of the eight Domains of Magic – Beasts, Heavens, Death, Fire, Metal, Shadows, Light or Life –, or practice a lesser known Knowledge, such as Natural Magic or Necromancy. You can now memorize Spells of the chosen Domain for the following XP price. Number of currently known Spells Cost in XP for a new spell Intelligence Bonus x 1 / 100 XP ,Intelligence Bonus x 2 / 200 XP ,Intelligence Bonus x 3 / 300 XP ,Intelligence Bonus x 4 / 400 PX … and so on. So, if your Intelligence Bonus is 4, the first 4 Spells will cost you 100 XP each, then 200 XP for the next 4, and so on. The complete rules for learning new Spells can be found in Chapter 8: Magic. Under normal conditions, you cannot learn more than one Arcane Magic (Domain) Talent. Also, you cannot learn the Blessed or Summoning Talents while you have the Arcane Magic Talent. You can unlearn this Talent for 100 XP, but if you do, you immediately lose all your Spells."

"You carry the spark of magic within you and have mastered the techniques to control it at the most basic level. When you take this Talent, you practice, and permanently memorize, a number of Spells equal to your Willpower Bonus. You can learn additional Minor Magic Spells for the following XP cost FMx1: 50, FMx2: 100, FMx3: 150... So, if your Willpower Bonus is 3 and you already have 3 Minor Spells, it will cost you 50 PX for the first one, then 100 PX for the next 3, and so on. Complete rules for learning new Spells can be found in Chapter 8: Magic."

"You are an undisputed master in your field, capable of creating works of such complexity that others can only remain silent and marvel at your genius. Each time you take this Talent, you can create an exceptional work of art with one of your Profession Skills. This work is unsurpassed in your field, a unique piece that will always impress, granting you bonuses, determined by the GM, most often to your Sociability Tests towards those familiar with your astounding work. Selling this coin will earn you at least ten times its normal value, and sometimes much more."

"You can move your hands with incredible dexterity. Passers-by do not benefit from any passive Perception Test to notice that you are using the Concealment Skill. Instead, they can only object to your Sleight of Hand Tests if they actively suspect you or are on the lookout for your moves. Additionally, attempts to use Melee (Brawl) to simply hit an opponent gain a bonus of +10 x your Dexterous Hands Level."
Talent.Test: " Dodge, Melee (Fight) to hit an opponent"

Talent.Explanation: "You have real creative talent. Add the Trade Skill associated with any Career you start. If the Profession Skill is already included in your Career, you can instead buy the Skill for 5 XP less per Increase."
