"You excel at taking on the appearance and mannerisms of others. With nothing but posture changes, facial twisting, and the judicious use of appropriate clothing, you no longer look like yourself without the need to use disguise kit, even while impersonating someone different sex."

"You are a master of dice games, and anyone who says you cheat is clearly wrong. When you successfully use Gamble or Dodge with dice, you can choose to either use the DR rolled or the units number of the die. So a successful roll of 06 can be used as a +6 DR. If you play real dice games to represent the one in play, always roll a number of extra dice equal to your Dice Mastery level and choose the best results."
Talent.Test: "Wager and Shoplift when playing a dice game"

Talent.Explanation: "You have accumulated years of combat experience, making it easy to keep weaker fighters at bay. For each time you have this Talent, you count as an additional person when calculating whether one side outnumbers the other. This Talent only comes into play when you are outnumbered. See page 162 for the rules regarding this case."

"When you have two weapons equipped, you can attack with both for your Action. Roll to hit with the weapon held by your primary hand. If you hit, determine Damage as normal, but remember to save your dice roll, as you will be using it again. If the first strike is successful, once resolved, the weapon in your off-hand can then target an available opponent of your choice using the same dice roll as the first strike, but reversed. So if you rolled 34 to hit with the first weapon, you get 43 to hit with the second. Remember to modify this second roll with your bad hand penalty (-20 unless you have the Ambidextrous Talent). This second attack is opposed to a new defense roll and the Damage for this second strike is calculated normally. One exception to this: if you roll a Critical for your first strike. If this happens, use the roll from the Critics table to serve as the roll for the second attack. So if you crit to the head and roll a 56 on the crits table and get a major eye wound, then your second attack would have a value of 56. If you choose to attack with both weapons, all your defensive throws suffer a -10 penalty until the start of your next Turn. You do not gain Advantage when you successfully hit or inflict a Wound on an opponent with Dual Wield unless both attacks hit."
Talent.Test: "Melee or Projectiles if attacking with two weapons"

Talent.Explanation: "You are an experienced freshwater navigator, accustomed to river vessels. You can ignore all penalties to your Tests when on board a boat that drifts due to whirlwinds, pitching ships, when you are off balance, and similar situations. Additionally, you count as two boatmen towards the minimum number of crew needed to run a river vessel."
"You have an imposing stature. When you use the Intimidate Skill, gain a DR bonus equal to your Threat Levels."

"Like Ranald the God of Deceit, you mix truth and lies as if there were no difference. When you use Charm to lie, listeners can’t counter it with their Intuition to detect if there’s anything questionable about what you’re saying."

"You are a particularly tough swimmer and accustomed to holding your breath for a long time underwater. Gain a bonus to your Endurance Bonus equal to your Endurance Swimmer Level to calculate the time you hold your breath."
"You are fabulously rich, and rarely short of cash. When you earn money (including with Income Activities), you earn +1 CO per number of times you have taken this Talent."

"You are an experienced businessman who knows how to close a deal. When you use the Bargain Skill, you reduce or increase the price of goods by an additional 10%. Note: The GM may impose a lower price reduction to show that a seller refuses to sell at a loss."

"You are descended from the nobility, or events during the game allowed you to rise there. Assuming you are dressed appropriately, you are always considered of a higher Status than others, unless they have the Nobility Talent. In this case, the Statuses are compared normally."
"You are a seasoned partier and know how to have fun. You can reverse the result of any failed Alcohol Resistance Test if it results in a success."
Talent.Test: "Charm and Gossip at parties, Alcohol resistance"

Talent.Explanation: "You are comfortable roaming the wilderness. When you use Stealth in a rural environment, those who cross your path do not get a passive Perception Test to detect you; they can only detect you if they are specifically stalking or looking for hidden people."

"You know the coins of the Old World well, and you are an expert in determining their value. You can judge the real value of a coin by your experience alone, without it ever requiring a Test. Additionally, you can identify counterfeit parts with a simple Benchmark Test; he is never opposed by the DR of the forger."
Talent.Test: "Evaluation to establish the value of coins"

Talent.Explanation: "You are the epitome of determination and resolve. Add your Stubborn level to your maximum Resolve pool."

"You are an experienced hunter and know all the best techniques for finding game. When traveling through game-rich regions, you are automatically able to hunt enough game to feed yourself and a number of people equal to your Hunter’s Eye level, as long as you have the time and the appropriate equipment. You can provide even more food using the normal Foraging rules (see page 131)."
Talent.Test: "Any Test to track or capture game"

Talent.Explanation: "You are a talented speaker and know how to galvanize large groups of people. Refer to the following table to see how many people you can influence with your Charm Skill (see page 119) when speaking in public. Number of people influenced 1:Normal x 5 ,2:Normal x 10 ,3:Normal x 20 ,4:Normal x 50 ,5:Normal x 100 ,6:Normal x 200 ,7:Normal x 500 ,8:Normal x 1000 .9: All who can hear your golden voice"

"You have perfect pitch, capable of perfectly reproducing notes and identifying them without ever needing to perform a Test. Additionally, add Entertainment (Singing) to any Career you start; if the Skill is already in your Career, you can instead buy the Skill for 5 XP less per Increase."
Talent.Test: "Entertainment (Singing), Language (Tonal languages, such as Elthárin, Cathayan, Magick)"

Talent.Explanation: "You are used to dealing with wounds quickly. If you fail a Heal Test while using Bandages, you can reverse the result if it results in a success; however, if you do, you can’t get more than +1 DR, as you’re focusing on speed rather than accuracy."

"You are good at being where enemy weapons are not. If you use Dodge to defend against an attack and win the opposite Test, you can move up to 2 meters as you dive out of range, meaning you are no longer Engaged. None of your opponents will gain a Free Attack when you sidestep."

"You are a very skilled fisherman and know the best ways to catch fish. Assuming a large enough body of water is available, you are automatically considered able to catch enough fish to feed yourself and a number of people equal to your Angler level, assuming you choose to pass. at least an hour or two with a line and bait. You can supply more fish using the normal Foraging rules (see page 131)."

"You never give up, even when tasks seem impossible. You can double the time that successful Resistance Tests allow you to endure a difficulty. This includes enduring prolonged riding, exposure, rituals, and similar issues."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Intelligence Stat (does not count as a Boost)."
"You are highly skilled in pharmacy, able to manufacture pills, balms, ointments, oils, creams, etc. You may reverse any failed Trade (Apothecary) Test if it results in a success."

"You are used to rolling oceans, and it is very unlikely that you will get seasick, even in the worst of storms. Under normal conditions at sea, you never need a Test to find out if you are seasick. In other cases (such as a storm or seasickness caused by magic), you can ignore all the penalties of the Tests to avoid this nausea."

"You are good at guiding ships through dangerous waters. If you fail a Test to cross them, you can reverse the result if it results in a success; however, if you do, you cannot get more than +1 DR, as you spot the impending danger at the last moment."
Talent.Test: " Rowing or Sailing tests as you navigate unsafe waters"

Talent.Explanation: "You are adept at wielding your shield to maneuver in combat so you can make the most of a desperate situation. When you use a Shield to defend yourself, you gain a number of Advantages equal to the number of Levels you have in Shieldbearer if you lose the opposite Test."
Talent.Test: "any Test to defend yourself with a shield"

Talent.Explanation: "Your presence fills others with awe and admiration. Your aura of authority is such that those with a lower Status cannot resist your Leadership Tests with their Willpower. Of course, enemies are still no more inclined to respect or obey you, but ordinary mortals rarely stand against you."

"You are used to anticipating the needs of others as well as your own. A number of times per session equal to your Foresight level, you can pull out of your backpack (or similar) the equipment necessary for the current situation, as long as its Encumbrance is 0, it is credible that you ’ve bought recently, and it’s not too implausible. It could be anything from a flask of alcohol to fortify an injured comrade to a cheap whistle absolutely necessary for a passing acrobat. Each time you do so, you must deduct the cost of the item taken out of your bag to offset the money spent earlier."

"You are comfortable in tunnels, sewers and any other underground environment. When you use Stealth there, those who cross your path do not get passive Perception Tests to detect you; they can only notice you if they are specifically stalking or looking for hidden people."
"You can reload ranged weapons with ease. You add a DR equal to your Rapid Reload level to any Test to reload a ranged weapon."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Agility Stat (does not count as Augments)."

"You are used to desperate fights, able to turn even the most dire situations to your Advantage. If you win the opposed Close Combat Test, instead of gaining +1 Advantage, you take all of your opponent’s current Advantages. In this case, you cannot inflict any Damage, even if it was your Turn in the Round."

"Your strong constitution makes it easier for you to survive a specific threat. You can automatically pass the first Test to resist the specified threat, such as Magic, Poison, Disease, Mutation, each game session. If the required DR is large, use your Endurance Bonus as the DR for the Test."
Talent.Test: "All those to resist the associated Threat"

Talent.Explanation: "The best defense is attack, so you respond to an attack with a lightning-fast counterattack. If your weapon has the Quick Perk, you can inflict Damage when attacked, as if it were your Action. You can Riposte a number of attacks per Round equal to your Riposte Level."

"You’re tough and take damage. You reduce all Damage taken by 1 per number of times you took the Tough Talent, even though Damage cannot normally be reduced. But you still suffer a minimum of 1 Wound from any source of Damage."

"You are brave or mad enough that the fear of certain enemies is a distant memory. With a single Accessible (+20) Calm Test, you can ignore the Intimidate, Fear, or Terror effects of the specified enemy when you encounter them. Common enemies include Beastmen, Greenskins, Outlaws, Vampires, Wardens, and Dissenting Sorcerers."
Talent.Test: "Calm to oppose Intimidation, Fear and Terror of your Enemy"

Talent.Explanation: "It’s hard to get you down. You can make an Intermediate (+0) Athletics Check to immediately land on your feet whenever you gain a Prone State. This Athletics Test is often modified by the Strength of the blow that knocks you down: for each +10 in Strength the blow has beyond your Toughness, you suffer a -10 penalty to the Athletics Test, and vice versa."

"You are exceptionally well-educated, and you possess a significant level of advanced knowledge in a field of study. You automatically know a number of correct pieces of information equal to your Scholar (Knowledge) Level, about a relevant question without needing a Knowledge Skill Test. Tests, as always, will give you more information, determined by the GM."

"You can fit in socially with the chosen group, as long as you dress and behave appropriately. Examples of social groups for this Talent are: Criminals, Cultists, Guilds, Nobles, Scholars, Servants, and Soldiers. If you don’t have the Talent, those who do will notice your discomfort in unfamiliar surroundings. This is primarily for character interpretation, but may provide a bonus to Fellowship Tests at the GM’s discretion."
"You can sense the shifting Winds of Magic, blowing from the Gates of Chaos to the poles of the world. You now have Second Sight (see page 233)."
Talent.Test: "any Test to detect Winds of Magic"

Talent.Explanation: "Your stern gaze and uplifting words inspire your soldiers to fight to the bitter end. Any subordinates able to see you may add your Warlord Level to the DR of one Willpower Test per Round. This bonus is not cumulative."

"One of your five main senses is particularly developed, allowing you to spot what others miss. You may make Perception Tests to detect details normally imperceptible through the associated sense, as determined by the GM. It could be: seeing an eagle beyond everyone’s field of vision, smelling an almost odorless poison, hearing the breathing of a motionless mouse in a wall, perceiving a faded letter in an engraving, or detecting that two beers of same brewer were drawn from two different barrels."
"You have an instinctive sense of direction. You automatically know where north is by looking at stars, trees, or any other familiar signs."

"You have a strange feeling when you are in danger, and can react accordingly. The GM can warn you that you are being watched, or that you are in danger; this will normally happen after a secret Intuition Test on your behalf. Additionally, you can ignore the Surprise if you pass an Intuition Test."
"You like to talk with others and it seems like they like to chat with you. You may reverse any Gossip Test if doing so allows the Test to pass."

"You are a self-taught Spellcaster who gradually figured out how to use magic, by trial and error. Add Language (Magick) to any Career you start; if it is already included in your Career, you can instead buy the Skill for 5 XP less per Increase. Additionally, you can spend a Resilience Point to cast (and memorize) a Spell from any Magic Domain, for 0 XP. You can do this a number of times equal to your Level in this Talent."

"You are agile as a cat, and able to fall from greater heights than others without injury. Each time you fall, perform an Athletics Test. On a success, reduce the fall distance by 1 meter, +1 additional meter per +1 DR rolled, to calculate the Damage."
"You are a very fast runner. Your Movement Attribute counts as 1 higher when you Run."
"You are a real bookworm. When using Search, you can reverse the result of any failed Test if it results in a success."
"You are a highly skilled corrupter. The GM can reduce the base cost of any required bribe by 10% per level you have in Bribery, down to a minimum of 10% of the original amount."
"You always hit an opponent right between the eyes... or where you intended to hit. Instead of flipping the die to determine which Location is hit with your ranged weapon, you can choose it."
"You are an exceptional marksman and know where to hit an enemy to deal maximum damage. Your Accurate Shot level is equivalent to bonus damage for all ranged weapons."

"If you have a loaded ranged weapon, you can fire outside of the normal Initiative order before any other fighter reacts in the next Round. You roll to hit using normal modifiers. Using Rapid Fire requires both your Action and Movement for your upcoming turn, which will count as having been spent during the next turn. If two or more Characters use Rapid Fire, the one who has taken this Talent the most times shoots first. In case of a tie, they fire simultaneously and should be managed at the same time."
Talent.Test: " Projectiles when performing a Rapid Fire"

Talent.Explanation: "You know how to find weak spots in a target’s armor. When you hit it, you can ignore a number of AP equal to your Safe Shot Level."
"You can deliver targeted shots with surgical precision. You ignore Projectile Test Difficulty modifiers due to the size of your target."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your Starting Fire Ability (does not count as Augments)."

"Distance is no obstacle to your Marksmanship skills, and you are adept at spotting targets both far and near. You suffer no penalties when shooting at Long Range, and half penalties at Extreme Range."

"A memorization technique initiated by the Cult of Verena, purportedly drawn from Elvish practices taught by the Lore-masters of Hoeth, Tower of Memories allows you to perfectly recall a series of events by memorizing them in an imaginary tower. You can remember a series of events of a length equal to your Intelligence without having to make a Test. For every 10 additional items you attempt to memorize, you must perform an Intelligence Test of increasing Difficulty to remember it correctly, starting from Very Easy (+60) for 10+, Easy (+40) for 20+, Accessible (+20) for 30+, etc. Beyond its obvious usefulness for Gambling, as this Talent adds a Bonus of +20 to +60, depending on the usefulness of memorization during the game in progress, the GM can, if necessary, apply Bonuses to other Tests . Each time you take this Talent, you can recall an additional series of events, without having to forget a previously memorized one."

"You are good at spotting and using traps. You can perform a Perception Test to spot them automatically, without having to tell the GM of your intention; the GM may prefer to perform these Tests secretly for you."
"Your mastery of a specific Profession is exceptional. You remove the level of your Skilled Worker Talent from the DR required for any Extended Test using your Occupation Skill."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Strength Stat (does not count as Raises)."
"You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Stamina Stat (does not count as Boosts)."

"You are good at playing and winning at cards, although your methods may involve a bit of cheating. When you successfully use Gamble or Sleight while playing cards, you can choose to either use the DR rolled or the units number from your die. So a hit of 28 can be used as a +8 DR. If you are playing with an actual deck of cards to represent what is happening in play, you may receive an additional number of cards per deal equal to your Cheating level, then discard some to return to the appropriate hand size before each round of game."
Talent.Test: "Wager and Shoplift when playing a card game"

Talent.Explanation: "When determining Damage, use your opponent’s Endurance Bonus as your Strength Bonus if it is higher; always determine this point before any other rule modifying your Strength or Strength Bonus. Additionally, if your target is larger than you, and you roll a Critical (see page 159), multiply all Melee Damage you inflict by the number of Size categories your target has above yours. (so, 2 categories = x2, 3 = x3, and so on); this multiplication is calculated after all modifiers have been applied. See page 342 for more information about Size."
"You gain +1 to your Movement Attribute."

"You are used to analyzing the battlefield to make quick decisions informed by the shifting waves of conflict. You can make an Intermediate (+0) Perception Test to ignore the Surprise, modified normally by the situation."

"You can see perfectly in natural darkness. Assuming you have at least a weak light source (such as starlight, moonlight, bioluminescence), you can see clearly up to 20 yards per Level of Night Vision. Additionally, you can extend the effective illumination distance of all light sources by 20 meters per level of Night Vision."

"You clearly see the great works of the gods all around you. You automatically know when you enter sacred ground, and can make an Intuition Test to receive visions (often obscure and interpreted via the paradigm of your cult or your individual belief system) regarding the locality if significant events have occurred. happened here in the past."
Talent.Test: "Intuition test when standing on sacred ground"

Talent.Explanation: "You gain a permanent +5 bonus to your starting Initiative Stat (does not count as Raises)."
"You are indomitable, and you will never willingly bow to others. Using the Intimidate Skill does not instill Fear in you and will not prevent you from opposing an intimidating interlocutor."

"You are a curious soul who has traveled everywhere, and learned all kinds of local information. Add Lore (Region) to any Career you start. If it is already included in the Career, you can buy the Skill twice – with a different Specialization each time, such as Altdorf, Vorbergland or Ubersreik – for 5 XP less per Increase."

"You are very resistant to magic. The DR of any Spell affecting you is reduced by 2 per point you have in this Talent. A Spell’s DR is only modified by the highest Magic Resistance Talent score in its target’s area. Additionally, you will never be able to learn the Blessed, Summon, Arcane Magic, Minor Magic, and Sorcerer! Talents."
"You are much shorter than most people in the Old World. Full rules for the different Sizes can be found in Chapter 12: Bestiary on page 342."

"At the age of 10, a Priest of Morr, also known as an Augur, took you aside to predict your death in an incense-heavy coming-of-age ritual called Destiny. In agreement with your GM, propose an appropriate Destiny. If your Character dies in a corresponding manner, your next Character will gain a bonus equal to half the total XP accumulated by your dead Character during the game."

"By accident or design, you have surrendered a part of your soul to one of the Dark Gods, and can now practice the infamous magics of Chaos. Your leader of Ruin immediately grants you access to a single Spell from the chosen Domain (usually the Domains of Nurgle, Slaanesh or Tzeentch) and you gain a Corruption Point when the Spell enters your mind, so as not to never come out again. When you take this Talent, which costs 100 XP each time, you learn another Spell of the chosen Domain and gain a Corruption Point. For more information on available Spells, see Chapter 8: Magic. Under normal conditions, you can only know one Chaotic Magic Lore."
"The creature is a large example of its species. It receives +10 Strength and Toughness, and –5 Agility"
"The creature feels no pain or can ignore it. All non-amputation penalties suffered from Critical Wounds are ignored, although Conditions are suffered as normal."

"No matter how hard the creature is hit, it gets back up. All Critical Wounds not resulting in death can be healed; just attach the requisite body parts to the correct places, perhaps with staples or large spikes to hold them in place, and it’s good to go. Even ‘death’ may be ‘healed’ if the appropriate parts, such as a lost head, are attached to the body. If death occurs and all parts are in place, it may attempt a Challenging (+0) Endurance Test requiring an SL of 6 at the start of every round for Toughness Bonus Rounds after death. If a Test is successful, the creature chokes back to life with 1 Wound"
"The creature dislikes the Target. See page 190 for Animosity rules"
"The creature loves to win a fight. As long as it has more Advantage than its opponent, it is Immune to Psychology"
"The creature gains Fear (0) to the Target. See page 190 for Fear rules"
"The creature can see in the dark as daylight"
"The creature is at home in water. It can add its Agility Bonus to the SL of all Swim Tests and move at full Movement through water."
"The creature is at home in the forests. In the woodlands, it adds its Agility Bonus to the SL of all Climb and Stealth Tests."
"The creature is cold-blooded and slow to react. It can reverse all failed Willpower Tests."
"The creature is especially stealthy. It adds a number equal to its Agility Bonus to the SL of all Stealth Tests."
"The creature is protected by armour or thick hide. It has Rating Armour Points on all Hit Locations."
"This trait represents creatures whose size differs from the game standard (i.e. roughly human sized). There are seven steps of Size, ranging from Tiny to Monstrous."

Specie.Explanation: "Humans being the most validated civilized race in the Old World. From the plains of the Estalian Kingdoms to the frozen provinces of Kislev, humans occupy every region of the continent, and they thrive there. The largest and most powerful human kingdom is the Empire, a patchwork of mighty provinces covered in seemingly endless forests. Located in the heart of the Empire, the Reikland is the richest and most cosmopolitan region."

Opinion.source: Reikäger Jungling, State Soldier from Altdorf

OPINIONS.Opinion: They've been our allies since Sigmar walked this very city; fought with them meself back in '05. Sure, they're a bit stubborn, seriously vindictive and pretty blunt, but I won't hear a word said against them.

If I gets meself the sort wot eats and smokes all day, then I'm happy as Ranald in catnip. It's when I get them without proper manners nicking me crockery or knives and forks: that I just can't abide! They're all smiles and shrugs when the watch come to pick 'em up, like they don't understand what they done wrong.

Yes, I do trade with them. And, no, don't be ridiculous, I've never been turned to a pillar of salt just by looking at them. Truly, I find them graceful and urbane. Proper civilised, I'd say. But, 'tween you and me, if Verena were to ask, I might also say I find them just… odd. So very intense. Like every deal we make really matters.
Elves of the forest you say? Ain't none of 'em around here, mate. You want to be goin' south to Bretonnia. I hear they gots loads of them, and that they're completely horrible!

Specie.Explanation: "Halflings are found all over the Reikland, working in the service of commerce in every town. An entire district of the Reikland’s capital, Altdorf, known as Haffenstadt, is even home to hundreds of extended halfling families helping out with restaurants, taverns, pipe shops, and a staggering number of traveling diners. Halflings are also very present in many villages of the Reikland, where they often work as employees of an inn or a farm. They are gregarious creatures, preferring to live in groups"

Opinion.source: 'Tubs' Samworth Rumster XVI, Pie-seller from Kalegan

OPINIONS.Opinion: Stiff-necked and pious, warlike and jealous… I could go on, but good manners halts me, and, besides, I like them, and they like me pies. As long as you keep away from their temples and the hard-liners, they're an open and pretty welcoming bunch. Good folk, and good for business.

Opinion.source: 'Lilly' Joseppinalina Hayfoot, Pedlar in the Reikland

OPINIONS.Opinion: My aunt Bessi was the greediest, as were six of her sons. But Bessi has nothing on them Dwarfs. Eyes grow as big as Mannslieb at even a scratch of gold. But, if you tell them that, they'll growl at you like you've taken the last honeycake, and start scribbling notes in one of their damned books about insulting their family honour or whatnot.

Opinion.source: 'Dainty' Cordelineth Brandysnap IV, Thief from Altdorf

OPINIONS.Opinion: I've seen them on the rivers in their white ships. How do they keep them so clean? And their hair… oh, their hair… it's like sunshine, it is. Snuck on a boat once to see what they do. Same as the rest of us, it seems, just more... earnestly.

Opinion.source: 'Jammy' Mercimaus Alderflower II, Scholar from Fielbach

OPINIONS.Opinion: Elves living in the woods? Don't be bloody ridiculous. Elves live in white towers and pretty boats over in Altdorf-town, you idiot.

Specie.Explanation: "Dwarves, or Dawi as they call themselves, are legendarily gruff and stubborn. Although the majority live in vast mountainside constructions, known as “fortresses“, most of the major cities and the capital of Reikland are also home to dwarven populations. Given their clannish nature, dwarves tend to cluster together, forming enclaves or neighborhoods wherever they settle. Many of the dwarves living in Reikland are the descendants of those who were driven from fallen fortresses centuries ago, but most still consider themselves dwarves of the Gray Mountains, though some have never seen a hill, and much less a mountain."

OPINIONS.Opinion: They're just not my kind of folk. Always smiling. Always fidgeting. Always talking. Always moving in big groups that just won't shut up! When they come in my store, I like to shoo them off with a broom. Really, what have they got to be so happy about? I just don't trust them.

Don't talk to me about those bloody bastards! Alrug Skycaster, my ultimate granduncle, was bloody betrayed in the bloody War of bloody Vengeance by those… those… ARGH! It's our clan's oldest grudge! Stood for thousands of bloody years!

My great grandfather thought logging forests on t'other side of the Grey Mountains would be lucrative. Ignored all the warnings, he was sure he was onto a winner. What could a bunch of skinny Elves do to him and his lads, after all? A lot, as it turned out. Only my grandfather survived, left alive to spread the message: "Keep out of their forests!

Specie.Explanation: "Tall and slender, with dainty pointed ears, most elves are blessed with long, thin hair and melodious voices. Although they may seem fragile, their physiology is not just powerful, but also extraordinarily agile and dexterous. There is little sexual dimorphism between elves, which often causes confusion in humans who interact with them."

OPINIONS.Opinion: I find these cheerful creatures genuinely interesting. I lived amongst an extended family group for a while, and found them so open, welcoming, and nurturing it was authentically touching. But, eventually, I had to move on, the smell was simply over-powering, and they have no understanding of personal space, which soon loses its charm.

If the Asrai would bother to look beyond their dirty noses, they would see what we are all up against. Isolationist idiots that deserve everything that's coming to them. I doubt the Eonir are any better.

Specie.Explanation: "Wood Elves are rare in Reikland, and for good reason. During the last days of the War of the Beard, many elves withdrew from the Old World. But a few remained and retreated into the depths of the magical forests, which they now call their home. Over three thousand years of isolation, hardship and war ensued, making the “wood elves“ culturally very different from their high elf cousins."

Opinion.source: Algwyllmyr Twiceseen, Seer from Athel Loren

OPINIONS.Opinion: I see hateful creatures with darkness in their hearts and a complete disrespect for order. But they are widespread, warlike, and, most importantly, easy to manipulate. Given winter draws near, it is time to use them.
More stubborn than the Oak of Ages, they understand one argument only: force. So, use it swiftly and decisively, and be aware they will return for petty vengeance at a later date.

Opinion.source: Alafael Harrowlay, Entertainer from the Laurelorn

OPINIONS.Opinion: I met one when travelling Middenland during the ninth year of Queen Marrisith. It talked a lot. And I do mean a lot. When we parted ways by a town it told me was named "Delberz", I found it had somehow managed to steal several pouches of herbs from my belt. I was impressed. So, I suggest not trusting the things, but the companionship and local lore they share may be worth the cost!

Opinion.source: Cynwrawn Fartrack, Hunter from the Laurelorn

OPINIONS.Opinion: Conceited beyond any sensible measure, don't approach the Asur. They are jaded, arrogant, and likely lost to Atharti. And if they try to look down on you in that superior manner they so prefer, just remind them their Queen in Avelorn lives a life no different to ours.

Career.Explanation: "Charismatic and a good talker, you defend your cause against the established order. “Believe me, if you want to eradicate the agents of the Doomspinners, follow the clamor of the streets. They cannot resist him. They will resurface, sooner or later.” - Adrian Hoven, Cleric-Captain, Knight of the Hearts of Fire. The Agitators lobbied for various political causes, using posters, demonstrations and public speaking. They win the sympathy and support of the poorer populations, but must be careful not to attract the attention of the conservative Sigmarites or dwarves. The most dangerous Agitators succeed in undermining the authority of nobles, cities, and sometimes even entire provinces. The Pamphleteers put up leaflets on billboards or distribute them in market places. The Agitators are constantly on the move, looking for large crowds or fleeing the authorities. They sometimes become leaders of heterogeneous groups, made up of homeless and revolted, urging them - while persuading them - to go and fight for a great cause. Fog and riots are legendary in Altdorf. Maybe it’s because it’s the Imperial Capital, or maybe it’s because the Gray College draws the squalls of the traitor Ulgu, the Gray Wind of Magic, there. Whatever the reason, when the mists from the plains of Altdorf fill the streets, the people rise up. Woe to the guards who would try to prevent him from being heard. Religious Agitators manage to make a living as street preachers, taking alms from the most devout worshipers, and attracting followers in the form of flagellants and fanatics. Agitators who survive long enough to become Demagogues are mostly supported by allies who remain in the shadows and seek to impose change on the motives, often known only to them."

"You are particularly gifted in chemistry and various preparations. You manufacture and sell drugs of all kinds. Apothecaries specialize in the preparation of medicinal treatments - most often pills, inhalations and ointments - which they sell either to the sick or to doctors. Their workshops are overflowing with impressive displays of bubbling stills, overflowing beakers, used pestles and mortars as well as paraphernalia for various physical preparations. Some Apothecaries make ends meet by selling illicit substances - from stimulants for beleaguered students to the weirdest hallucinogenic herbs for idle nobles, or when fulfilling shady orders for even larger groups. shady. It is a very lucrative but dangerous business. The rarest ingredients are expensive, which is why Apothecaries often run into cash flow problems and go off on their own to explore the wilderness to find their own ingredients. Many of them accept short-term missions within certain mercenary or military expeditions, which earns them a few extra coins. Due to the pressure imposed by the guild of Doctors, most cities refuse that Apothecaries practice medicine, but this does not prevent them from taking on the role of healers during the game. They are very versatile, proving to be able to identify uncommon and potentially dangerous substances that the party may stumble upon and even turn some of them into useful medicines. “The chemistry of men? As rudimentary as their architecture. It will kill you! I once asked for an invigorator after a rough night of drinking. I got food poisoning that lasted a week! - Thorica Norrasdotr, Dwarf Merchant"

"You are a highly skilled artisan who takes pride in your work, and you create products to sell while fulfilling specific orders. “You must understand, my boy, that the wines of Wurtbard have a reputation to uphold. It looks like this bottle went through the barrel of a Hochland rifle. This is downright unacceptable. - Dame Glasmeister, Guild Master of the Glassblowers Artisans craft everything from the everyday goods produced by bakers and shipbuilders, to the weapons and riverboats crafted by blacksmiths and shipwrights. The largest towns and cities of the Empire have guilds to protect their Artisans from scammers, as their entire Career can be jeopardized by unskilled competitors who are selling low-quality goods on the sly. Guild Masters meet quality standards, and those who don’t meet them get kicked out and banned from practicing in town. Artisans in full apprenticeship can be sent to other masters. The pressure that pushes them to perfection is so heavy to bear that some of the youngest Artisans sometimes take breaks in order to turn to less oppressive structures, such as the Army or the Navy. Dwarf guilds generally do not accept humans, and dwarves are usually allowed to practice their profession in Imperial cities without needing to join a local guild. This can become a source of conflict, as guilds are generally very reluctant to accept talented competitors. Halflings aren’t as picky and will happily join human guilds (if accepted there) and similarly allow humans to join theirs. Elves don’t have Craftsmen’s guilds, and even if they could join one, they’re unlikely to stoop to one. Artisans intervene at all levels of society, because they manufacture goods, but also repair others. They are hired by navies to maintain fleets, by armies to manage war machines and siege engines, and by Chambers of Commerce of all sizes to turn raw materials into salable goods."

"You have an innate artistic talent, one that transcends everyday life and uplifts the souls of others. Artists use their talents - in painting, sculpting, writing or otherwise - to create exquisite works of art. Often, they begin their Career as Art Students with renowned Artists, even if some are already pure prodigies. Some patrons will take the most talented under their thumb while others will turn to teaching, finding themselves at the head of their own school, and bringing donors among the richest in their art galleries at the fashion. Attracting the appropriate patrons is not always easy, and this is the reason why Artists of all backgrounds find themselves on the roads looking for the rare pearl. Even those with enough to support themselves travel the world in search of new sights to paint, silhouettes to sculpt, or inspiration. It is very often the most distant churches, abbeys and temples that seek to commission sacred frescoes or bas-reliefs. Unfortunately, most Artists spend their lives trying to prove their worth to a society that rarely appreciates them. The latter manage difficult ends of the month in various ways: they ridicule nobles and politicians in caricatures which they publish in Altdorf newspapers, make composite portraits of suspects for the captains of the guard, write societal comments or indulge in counterfeiting the work of renowned artists."

Item.name: Bag containing tools of the profession (Artist)

Career.Explanation: "You are a local official trusted by the rulers of the region to effectively and firmly administer their lands. “I’m going to take a look myself at the pasture in question. Until I return, I want no argument between your turbulent descendants, am I clear enough, Bauer, Meier? And you’ll split the cost of repairing the inn, or you’ll have to forfeit anything you may or may not have a right to on these lands. - Lorenz Schulte, Prefect of the Elster Valley The Nobles entrust the Baillis with collecting taxes from their lands. Some Bailiffs are respected and honest, and hardly a week goes by without them visiting a Temple of Sigmar. Others are tyrants who use the power granted by their lord over their properties and possessions to make use of threats and violence when carrying out their profession. Baillis who have been in office for a long time often become loyal servants of the ruling family and have substantial benefits in kind. The Prefects benefit from a greater field of action and have greater responsibilities. They ensure the maintenance of order at the level of the borders of the territory of their lord and resolve conflicts, whether they originate from cattle stories or the limits of agricultural properties. The vast majority of Baillis have some freedom, allowing them to take the time to attend to private matters or hire others to do so on their behalf. Since there are just as many of them who have full authority over the territories they care for, they are regularly sent by their employers to solve various problems, which can lead them to the most unexpected places."

"You navigate the treacherous waters of the Old World, alternately carrying passengers or cargo, while relaying breaking news. “Watch out for the fork. It’s the barge driver who has the bottle who tells you that. If you are approaching a rock or other danger, follow the direction of the stars and make sure to stay in that direction, or take the direction of the forest and be careful to stay on course. Otherwise, you risk drifting and sinking. And no one wants to lose their barge. - Jacob Walles, Barge Operator who sank his at a spur Countless boats and barges roam the waterways of the Empire, transporting goods from the farthest corners of the provinces to the greatest cities. These flat-bottomed ships are able to navigate against the current much more easily than others, and an extensive network of canals allows them to reach the most remote places. The Captains are seasoned sailors who know the rivers they take perfectly. A Boater is still just a minion, but it won’t be long before he learns the ropes. Boatmen pilot merchant ships laden with goods to and from markets, and are either self-employed or work for a larger chamber of commerce. Many Boatmen are also ferrymen, carrying their passengers across rivers to or from towns. In the most important cities, some also pilot river taxis, are at the head of pleasure boats or convoy ships on behalf of a third party. A Boatman will not need to go ahead of the adventure, because it is it which will not fail to present itself to him. Everyone needs boats, especially those who go on an adventure. In addition, these skiffs make an excellent base of operations. The Boatman will not even have to know if the objectives of the adventure will require leaving the banks of the river or not. And even if that were temporarily the case, adventurers could easily allow a skilled Boatman to mind their business while they take a break from their river expedition."

"Ambitious and socially mobile, you are the glue that unites urban society. The Bourgeois are part of a growing class of citizens with both time and money. Many take one or two days off a week and can easily adapt to a life of adventure between shifts or after hours. Some may wish to go further, and if a Bourgeois has some cash to spare, it should be easy to negotiate a time off with an employer. It is very common for citizens of the Empire to go on pilgrimage for weeks or months. Skilled workers are always in demand, and there will most certainly be a vacancy when they return. The Bourgeois satisfied the flourishing centers of commerce and the demand for workers. They fill various roles for private craftsmen or municipal councils: bankers, employees, street vendors, innkeepers, newsagents, stable boys, stall keepers, gatekeepers, cleaners, and many others. Their pay rates vary: some may haggle for an extra commission, while civilian employees like lamp attendants and gatekeepers receive fixed salaries. They have few opportunities for promotion, but those with determination, common sense and luck can eventually own or run their own business. The most prosperous Burghers often join town councils that oversee civil affairs, with Burgomasters - the most important town leaders - often enjoying the same social status as Merchant Princes and Guild Masters."

"“An escort came yesterday to make sure we were safe. My God, he was so handsome and so dashing. Who wouldn’t be tempted to ride with him? He grabbed my buns and sped like the wind. He’ll never pay them, I suppose. - Lena Fluffe, baker in Walfenburg A dashing and fearless cavalryman, you bring speed, versatility and dexterity to the handling of weapons on the battlefield. Whether within units of gunslingers, escorts, demi-lancers, mounted archers, or similar, Cavaliers are deployed to gain maximum strategic advantage. In the campaign, this means scouting, attacking, harassing enemy lines, or defending peasants. On the battlefield, they are also particularly versatile, able to strike quickly and disperse. When it comes to velocity, cueing, versatility, and sheer momentum, no one equals the Cavaliers. Very fast, light cavalry are employed by many armies, including cult armed forces and other less formal groups, such as private militia mercenaries. Bretonnian armies employ mounted men-at-arms, while Wood Elf Knights are among the most feared light horsemen in the Old World. A Cavalier serving in the Imperial Army isn’t going to drop everything on a whim. If they have a goal that they wish to pursue personally, they will have to obtain permission from their superior officers, buy out their commission if they have one, or go absent without leave. They may also be ordered to investigate important matters by their superiors. Mercenary Horsemen have more freedom to adventure, being little more than just swords for hire."

"Unscrupulous and charming, you separate fools from their money; and thank God, there is no shortage of fools… A Charlatan operates in confidence, but makes his money from betrayal. By preying on emotional and psychological weaknesses, Charlatans offer their “target” a prize that is too good to be true. Social privileges do not provide protection, and even the most noble citizens can fall into the nets of a skilled Charlatan. Lack of scruples, combined with a gift for lying, also benefits Charlatans. “Lord Schwalb’s last living heir, you say?“ Bullshit! You are the fifth “heir“ to pass this afternoon! How much did you pay for this piece of paper? And above all, who is the scammer who sold it to you? - Gerold Behn, Annoyed Butler To avoid raising suspicion, Charlatans rarely stay in one area for long. Few Tricksters openly confess their vocation, preferring to pretend to be someone else. Very few reasons therefore prevent Charlatans from pursuing parallel interests; they can then go back anywhere rich fools are willing to pay for nothing but a promise. Charlatans include Tricksters, Scammers, and other Crooks seeking to attack the credulous. Halflings often commit scams in small family groups. The young high elves, slumming with humans, regard their scams as a great hunt, motivated not by profit, but by proving their superiority. Some experienced Charlatans work with artists, who falsify documents for a share of the profits."

Item.name: an assortment of colored powders and water
an assortment of charms and trinkets

Career.Explanation: "Independent and tough killers who earn their living by selling the flesh and fur of wild creatures. Are you telling me that hunting is not a sport because both parties don’t know it’s just a game? May I then suggest to you that you may be in the wrong game? - Graf Bernard Leutze von Holthusen “May Taal reward you“ is a common courtesy in Hochland, where the locals are proud of their hunting tradition that dates back to the Age of Sigmar. Most people in the Empire hunt, whether it’s a hobby, a profession, or a necessity, and Hunters frequently engage in poaching when times get tough. The amputation of two fingers is one of the most common penalties applied to a hunter caught poaching. Realizing that they will never be able to shoot archery again, the vast majority of them will flee before being captured and thus avoid the sentence, preferring to try their luck in the forest. Around the fertile villages of southern Vorbergland, the Hunters are losing ground due to the felling of trees by peasants and the hunting reserves imposed by the nobles. The Imperial Army is always on the lookout for reliable Hunters to join its ranks on campaigns where they take on the role of archers or scouts. A Hunter interested in hard cash will always find an adventure that suits him. The most talented Hunters regularly hold the position of huntsman for the nobility, which gives them access to quality weapons, horses and even hawks. Elves and dwarves have no regard for the borders of men and will not hesitate to venture deep into the lands of the latter in search of difficult prey. Stories of the wild hunts of the Wood Elves terrify the children of the Gray Mountains, and not without reason, for if ever an intruder gets too close to the lands of the Elves, then the hunter quickly becomes the prey."

"Determined and ruthless, you pursue your prey relentlessly: for justice or for money. Bounty Hunters, depending on the criminal they are looking for, must sometimes take the paths of adventure. As they are completely autonomous, it is easy for them, temporarily, to put aside their objective and take on another mission if it arises. Moreover, since the skills they master are very often sought after, it often happens that Bounty Hunters definitely turn to a life of adventure, renting out their talents for payment. The Bounty Hunter Career is a great starting Career, as it perfectly blends Social Skills and combat, allowing you to be useful no matter what. Bounty Hunters pursue fugitives, or outlaws, for money. Most are legally appointed by provincial courts and given warrants that give them the right to capture, and sometimes even kill, their target. While some are motivated by Verena’s justice, most are still more drawn to the rewards and find that the “death“ of “dead or alive“ makes it possible to get rich even faster. Most Bounty Hunters start out as Thieves Hunters, who are hired by victims of looting in order to find their stolen goods. Over time, those who have earned a good reputation sometimes manage to find regular work with merchants, nobles, guilds or other cults, or even start a company of Bounty Hunters and work as a team in order to recover the maximum. of rewards."

"Rushing into battle on a heavy steed, you dominate the battlefield, spreading fear in your path. Many believe that the main warriors of the Old World are the heavy cavalry. A massed charge is an impressive sight, but even a single Knight can represent an army on his own. There are many orders of chivalry in the Empire, the most famous being the Reiksguard, White Wolves, Knights Panther and Knights Griffin, each with their own glorified history and powerful heroes. Many Knights of the Empire belong to secular orders of chivalry, in part because heavy spear training is too expensive for most nobles. Templar orders, those who devote their services to a single deity, are just as widespread, but a little more independent. Among them are countless freelancers, mercenary knights, and dishonored knights, most selling their spears to the highest bidder. “Lady Myrmaelia Jaeke is the finest knight in the Order of the Blazing Sun. How can I be sure? Well, I held that title, and she beat me. - Birgitte van der Hoogenband, Abbess-General of the Monastery of the Black Madonna, former Knight of the Blazing Sun accompany an impatient heir across the Empire. In the same way, the Templars will have to fulfill the wishes of their god. All of this provides perfect opportunities for Knights to go on an adventure. In comparison, for an independent, the adventure life is what he follows by default."

Item.name: large unit of Knights/several small units of Knights

Career.Explanation: "Obstinate, you lead your passengers safely, ensuring their safety, despite the permanent dangers you face. For many people, the stagecoach is the only way to travel from one city to another. Though the wilderness traversed to your destination will be crawling with beastmen, bandits, and worse, a brave and tenacious Coachman, whose horses are fresh and the trusty blunderbuss loaded, can make this journey possible. In order to avoid risks as much as possible, stagecoach relays are in constant search of speed, and their employees, trusting no one, are preceded by a reputation for harshness among travellers. Coachmen most often begin as Postilions, mounted on the lead horse of a team, and in all weathers. Some Coachmen carry letters instead of passengers, work as chauffeurs for certain nobles, drive horse-drawn carriages or wagons full of goods, or find themselves in larger cities piloting the omnibuses. Finally, some become accomplices to escape. “Three days ago, I was stuck in Weissbruck during the storms. Nothing was going or coming. Just when I thought I was going to miss my appointment in Bögenhafen, I saw three stagecoaches appear on the frozen track at the same time. So classic! You wait for days, and suddenly three come! - Stelle Grabbe, Merchant Good Coachmen are highly sought after for unusual, dangerous or illegal requests. A coachman looking to change his routine will take advantage of winter to take a break, as long journeys see a sharp drop in this season. Transport companies are reluctant to hire experienced drivers. It is therefore easy for them to find work."

"Full of wisdom and free from interference, you travel across the Empire to sell your goods wherever you want, without hindrance. “You have a unique work of art here that you will never see anywhere else. On the other hand, if you want more, I have a dozen in the back of my cart. - Delberz Trötte, Trader Les Colporteurs travel from village to hamlet, offering goods and services such as knife sharpening, darning and other handicrafts. Most carry relatively inexpensive goods that are readily available in larger cities, such as ribbons or hairpins. Peddlers are always welcome, even among the most suspicious people, because everyone likes to acquire trinkets and trinkets, even if they are superfluous. A Peddler with even the slightest bit of ambition is bound to be interested in stories that claim how easy it is to make money in the most remote lands. As they rely only on themselves, it is easy for them to accompany any group of adventurers, and take advantage of the road to earn a few coins. They also have the possibility of being opened the doors of various fortresses and other camps without being asked the slightest question. Some Colporteurs also take on the job of messenger; others perform the de facto role of town crier, spreading gossip and news to the quieter corners of the Empire in exchange for food and lodging. Because of the dangers lurking on the roads, Peddlers prefer to work with a stall in a town market. You can also come across them on pilgrimage routes, living off the sale of relics to devotees."

"Wisdom and very knowledgeable, you provide advice and assistance that will ensure the prosperity of your clients. Advisors provide advice to those who employ them. They are very aware of the social and political conditions of their employer’s domain and hold a great deal of confidential and sensitive information. While many Advisors are passed on from generation to generation, others are actively seeking noble clients in order to achieve a certain level of wealth and power. Some young heirs will appoint a childhood friend or university friend, in whom they have blind confidence, as the first Assistant. If something abnormal or dangerous is happening on their employer’s estate, then an Advisor is in the best position to investigate. At the highest Career levels, a Consultant or Chancellor will have their own trusted staff they can rely on to look after their affairs during a short absence. Advisors can approach different categories of people, including the most difficult to access, and are already in a position where they are expected to ask questions on behalf of their employer. Long years spent at court or in the service of a minor nobleman are necessary to achieve the highest responsibilities. Many advisors have chosen not to serve the nobility, but instead offer their wide range of knowledge to criminals, warlords, merchants, cults or even guilds."

"You smuggle cargo, seeking to avoid taxes and dodge river patrollers in order to cash in the maximum profit. “Listen, this is where we will put the best bottles of Bordeaux. The river patrollers will search behind, find them and confiscate them. And that’s what we want, because that means they’re not going to find the twelve bottles that we hid under there. And if they ever found them, it wouldn’t be the end of the world because they’d be so happy with their catch that they wouldn’t even look where we hid twenty-four other bottles. - Hansel Solomon, Smuggler Trade is taxed by local lords, just as it is taxed, but illegally, by bandits and racketeers. Smugglers see themselves as good souls: Merchants make better profits, customers pay less, River Patrollers, less suffocated by morality, take a small commission, outlaws are avoided, at a minimum. A good dose of ingenuity and a bit of a bottle are needed to avoid bailiffs, official customs, tax collectors and anyone who will try to stop them. But the Smugglers accept this risk-taking, because they have to provide for themselves and their families. Quite often, Smugglers find themselves embroiled in adventures even if they generally seek to keep everything as calm as possible. Many adventures can occur during a smuggling mission, and even if everything goes well, there will always be the temptation of the next mission, bigger and even more lucrative than the previous one. There are a lot of solo adventures that can be had with smuggling missions alone. It is also easy for a Smuggler to find work that deviates from what he usually does. Those who have more than one trick up their sleeve, the watchful eye, and who is able to maintain their composure, even when the situation gets complicated, will always be a recruit of choice for any dangerous expedition. There are all kinds of Smugglers: some will carry small but very valuable items for noble families, while others will convey huge cargoes for more or less shady merchants. Some also smuggle illegal goods, and this is a crime for which the penalty is far greater than a simple burnt finger or receiving the Smuggler’s mark."

"Even if you unload goods from ships for a fee, everyone knows that it’s the Longshoremen who rule the docks. “My boy, don’t believe that longshoremen take it easy. It’s dangerous work, in confined spaces, with very heavy loads and endless stacks of boxes, and if done incorrectly, the cargo could become unbalanced and cause the boat to capsize. What I want to tell you is that you have to pay them properly. And if you want to see a sinking ship, add some coins. - Aleida Fuchs, Merchant Although their only job is to load and unload ships, Dockworker guilds have the power to slow or speed up trade. Which gives them a certain power, because a lot of docks are run by these guilds. In larger cities, there may be violent clashes between several gangs to decide which will have power. Scowling Foremen run the day-to-day business of the guild when they’re not whistling their gangs out of dockside taverns when a new ship arrives, or defending their turf. . Despite the monotony and repetition that govern life on the quays, certain opportunities for adventure are offered to a Stevedore. Some gangs literally rule the roost and won’t hesitate to fight to defend every inch of their turf. Longshoremen are interesting Characters to have on hand, as they are very resourceful and are used to dealing with the poor. A Longshoreman can work alone in a riverside village, or belong to a larger gang that works on a bustling wharf. Sometimes he can even find himself in a gang of organized criminals who will do this work as a cover. Some decide to become executors, and make sure everyone is working to their maximum."

"In your hands trained to wield it with deadly precision, your blade is an instrument of justice inherited from the oldest tradition. Duelists fight on behalf of others - settling any honor issues between individuals or organizations, or act as a representative of the law, taking the side of the accused or defender in trials resulting in judgment by combat . For some Duelists, fighting is reward enough for the risks they take. The training is dangerous, and leaves some novices disabled or disfigured for life. Those who live long enough to learn from their mistakes can hope to become Master Duelists and teach their unstoppable techniques to eager students. Champions of Justice fight for nobles and governments, and the fate of entire nations rests upon their blades. Some more advanced Duelists, including warm-blooded Altdorf students, prefer pistols. What older generations find disrespectful as well as silly. “In my defense, sir, he was the first to draw blood. - Rosabel Viernau, Duelist “Make sure Doctor Schuller is there.“ deny? Good question. Pay her up front, be courteous to her, and she’ll look the other way. So she won’t see anything until the duel is over, regardless of the outcome. - Sharp Blade Aleksandr Amblestadt’s advice to his students. Duelists, both seasoned and new, roam the Empire in search of opponents to enhance their reputation. For others, searching for an experienced teacher leads them to explore the most remote places of the Old World. Master Duelists practicing Exotic techniques are also highly sought after by Duelists hoping to add unique fighting styles to their repertoire. Duelists, who are seasoned fighters, regularly improve their lifestyle by becoming mercenaries, sometimes even going so far as to ensure the protection of caravans or ships. Although dwarves are not used to fencing with ridiculous swords and have no interest in the frivolities surrounding duels, resolving disputes through combat is an ancient tradition for them and they do not will therefore not hesitate to set off on a journey to become even better."

"Fearless and resourceful, you lead others through the dangerous wilderness of the Old World “I don’t think you want to descend the cliff road without a guide. There are human-sized traps that have been placed by the prefect to capture poachers. It almost cut off old Billi’s leg last week. - Gwyn, Eclaireur In a population where illiteracy is widespread and where maps are very rare, knowing the region you are in can, for travelers, make the difference between life and death. Pathfinders are experts at finding safe routes through the darkest corners and muddy roads of the Empire. Local guides will accompany their clients, warning them of possible dangers, sharing village gossip with them and showing them the best places to find food. The most experienced Pathfinders will most often remain invisible to their employers, because they will always be upstream exploring the avenues to come, and trying to spot possible dangers. While most Pathfinders dwell in lands they are familiar with, some specialize in escorting lands not yet mapped. Some Explorers sometimes even go so far as to venture into dangerous and hostile territories. Pathfinders are an invaluable aid to a group of adventurers, especially when they are setting out to seek their fortune for the first time. Coureurs des bois with solid knowledge may be asked to act as Scouts, although many of them remain solitary, going back and forth in the woods to warn of possible ambushes or spot enemies who would be further forward. to fill in the blanks on their cards. The majority of Pathfinders will not face danger themselves, preferring to retreat discreetly to warn their companions and ensure that their employer is not helpless in the face of the approaching threat."

Item.name: saddle cast with food for two weeks

Career.Explanation: "An emissary for whom the art of speaking is second nature, you do not hesitate to travel everywhere in order to negotiate advantageous treaties and pacts. “So look at her. She has a forked tongue like that of a snake and no scruples. Moreover, she cannot resist either elven wine or seductive footmen. I’m sure you can organize something…scandalous. - Odmar Horst, Guild Emissary Emissaries, who are experts in negotiation and social interaction, act as agents serving the interests of the Empire, a regional state, a foreign country or even a Chamber of Commerce. Intrigues are legion at court, and a Career choice like this is always risky, and becomes even more so in the high spheres of government. Although they generally have a kind of diplomatic immunity regarding the laws and customs of the countries they are visiting, Ambassadors must negotiate with caution. “My advice to Your Imperial Majesty is to keep this important business relationship with Karak Ziflin, so grow your beard and keep your promises. - Letter sent to the High Lord of the Presidency, written by Ambassador Willemijna von Kotzdam The Emissaries travel widely, cross paths with many people from all different backgrounds and extend their relations throughout the Old World. They are sometimes expected to get their hands dirty in order to satisfy the wishes of their masters. If failure does not mean immediate death, they may sometimes have to flee. First, Emissaries will have to prove themselves as Heralds, assisting Diplomats by negotiating the tedious minutiae of certain agreements, or representing merchants, guilds or cults, and improving their reputation with each pact. concluded. Some Emissaries get hired by mercenary companies; the best of them are able to make money for their employers without even a drop of blood being shed."

"Astute as well as suspicious, you investigate the heart of crimes in order to find answers. “We can deduce, from the sight of this door shattered into a thousand pieces, that the thief received help from a huge creature. But said creature could never have descended by this narrow staircase. This leaves us with only two possible conclusions. Either she materialized out of thin air, or our thief is a shapeshifter…” - Zavant Konniger, “Sage-Detective” Most Investigators deal with cases of theft of private property, missing persons, or murder , even if some investigate the headlines of the newspapers or even the cases of blackmail to get a little “bonus“. Investigative techniques include tracking footprints, cross-checks, logical deductions, and, if necessary, illegal searches. While secular Investigators act at the edge of the law for institutions like chambers of commerce, religious investigators, mostly in the service of Sigmar and Verena, follow a very strict code of ethics. “I imagine you are aware that I am the greatest detective in the world. You’ve heard of Alphonse before, right? - Alphonse Hercule de Gascoigne, tiny Breton detective Investigators are sometimes hired to solve mysteries that it would be too dangerous to try to solve alone, which can become an informal way to create a group of adventurers. Of course, the nature of these mysteries can mean that once one of them is solved, another arises. Some Investigators can therefore benefit from a stable job, provided that they are able to identify the potential clients behind each new mystery they uncover. Seasoned Investigators sometimes abuse sleeve effects to improve their credibility. Some Master Investigators present themselves as “observation specialists” and pride themselves on possessing talents that cannot be learned. It takes a healthy dose of self-promotion to rise to the rank of Detective and be offered deals across the Old World."

"Resourceful and self-interested, you make a living selling illicit goods in the city’s slums. “Laugh all you want, but those clothes cost a fortune. For a kid born under a manure heap, he lives a life of luxury. - Hertel Netzhoch, Innkeeper Matchmakers guide people to establishments offering a variety of illegal and immoral services. Although many humans and dwarves oppose such activities, most halflings and high elves are perfectly neutral when it comes to drug dens, brothels, and other houses of vice. Matchmakers living in urban areas sometimes travel to escape pestilence and religious persecution, the latter being more common in regions dominated by the Cult of Sigmar. Others, like those who roam with acrobats, consider travel an integral part of their profession. Those who manage to convince patrons can benefit from a lot of time to devote to their own fate. Matchmakers include drug dealers, strippers, prostitutes and models. Many of the famous masterpieces of the modern era were modeled after Matchmakers snatched from the streets. The armies on the move are followed by canteens, among whom the Matchmakers seek to make money by all means. Leaders, owners of establishments where Matchmakers congregate, can find themselves at the head of important empires providing services to all kinds of rogues, from fences who need to meet discreetly wealthy clients, to providing hideouts safe for gang leaders and crime lords."

"You dedicate your life to perfecting your knowledge, regardless of the paths you have to take. Erudites generally study at one of the institutions of learning in the Old World, among which of course is the University of Altdorf. Most specialize in one or two subjects, and many learn just enough to enable them to pursue a useful trade or provide them with enough knowledge to feel comfortable during a conversation at a social dinner. . Poorer Scholars often act as scribes, reading and writing letters for others, as most citizens of the Empire are illiterate. Others become preceptors and instruct the wealthiest families. Poorer Scholars who cannot or do not want to teach will often need to find funds to fund their research. Some will seek long-forgotten secrets or very old works in the most remote corners of the world. Others are hired to accompany groups of adventurers aware that their knowledge could be very useful. The most talented Scholars are regularly invited by universities to join their ranks, institutions where renowned Professors give lectures in front of hundreds of Students. Dwarves and High Elves are less likely to find themselves stationed in Imperial institutions, yet they travel the Empire in search of arcane knowledge. Scholar is a very useful Career, as it provides access to extremely rare Knowledge Skills, and provides a great way for the GM to share information with Players. If played with a modicum of common sense, the Scholar can temper the somewhat brutal and belligerent tendencies of the other Characters who solve all problems with swords. Scholars can use their knowledge to solve puzzles or craft out-of-the-ordinary strategies and tactics."

"You are the eyes and ears of another, revealing secrets and lies. Throughout the Old World, Spies are found serving well-known organizations. During their investigations, the Spies find themselves involved in intrigues which can be without risks, or much more sinister. They are often forced to flee when their identity, or their allegiances are revealed. These individuals use their skills in disguise to hide their true nature and avoid capture. More than one Spy has found himself going on an adventure after joining a group of heroes who will have taken him into their group despite themselves during an escape attempt. Spies are brave (or reckless) people who secretly go fishing for information for their clients. A well-infiltrated spy becomes a tremendous asset to anyone seeking information on an adversary’s activities. They spend months, even years, shaping a most mundane identity and establishing links with one or more groups of individuals. Every action they take is risky. Even if captured, Spies are rarely immediately executed; more often than not, they are tortured for a long time. Many Informants are forced, by blackmail or other form of threat, to practice espionage. A talented spy will earn a good living, but it is even more difficult to put an end to this kind of activity than to continue the practice. Because Spies will do anything to avoid attracting attention, they are very rarely preceded by their reputation, unless that reputation turns out to be as anonymous as themselves."

"The rivers are the nerve center of Old World commerce, and you live right in the middle of this anthill. “They say you can travel the whole empire if you stay on the Reik long enough. Well, I stayed there for twenty years, watching the current. I’ve seen things. I have seen many wars, and I have seen peace. I have witnessed good times and tougher times. I saw the joy, and the sadness. And, during all this time, I can tell you, in all honesty, that I did not catch a single fish. - Thys Lange, Reikland’s worst fisherman The fertile banks of the great rivers of the Empire are very heavily populated, and the inhabitants who work day and night on the waters and in the nearby marshes provide the vast majority of the fresh fish, eels and crustaceans that will help feed the neighboring towns and cities. Unlike the villages located inland, foreigners, who come to trade or deliver, are very numerous in the coastal villages. The Women of the River are therefore very versatile and very often the first to hear news from distant lands. Rivers are providers of many different trades. Many are those who harvest the riches of the Reik: fishermen (who use rods, spears or nets), eel hunters (who use traps) or even divers for shellfish. Most live in the riverside villages, dredging the riverbeds, towing and maintaining the thousands of ships that travel the Reik. A River Woman feels at home when she is near a body of water, and the extent of her skills are such that she can afford to stop working whenever she wishes, because she will be able to find work anywhere else if she needs it. A Woman of the River will be one of the first to hear the gossip that enamels the less frequented corners of the banks of a river and can even have interesting contacts among the most deprived. Their experience and knowledge can make the difference between success and failure on a river expedition."

"When you had lost all hope, your suffering and the virtue of Sigmar saved you! “We had Flagellants that came through the village a few months ago. They were terrifying: agony, pain, suffering. This is how we felt just looking at them. We didn’t know what to do. We knew we had to open our doors, welcome them, feed them and pray with them. But we eventually hid in the cellar until they were gone. Scary! -Wulfrum Barth, Villager Forgiveness is not easy, and is only won through hard work, pain, and respecting Sigmar’s will. Flagellants roam the Empire, whipping themselves in penance for their sins and those of others. They are determined to remain in the service of Sigmar until the end of the world, which they believe is imminent. Good people are supposed to welcome them, help them, feed them and pray with them. “ The end is near ! - Sign very often carried by Lashers. Most Lashers travel in large groups and are led by a Prophet of Doom who interprets Sigmar’s will. Some escort armies, whipping each other into a frenzy when a battle comes and fighting without worrying about their own safety. Others wander solitary, convinced that they will serve Sigmar most effectively by fighting the evil he places in their paths. It’s not hard for a Lasher to find themselves on an adventure, especially if it involves enemies of Sigmar. The Flagellants can then behave as usual, relying on the honest people of the Empire to offer them food, drink and shelter as they shuffle towards the end of all things."

"Your job is simple: keep the undesirables out. The best way to protect something is to post a guard there. Keeping guard can seem quite easy, it’s usually just about standing and not doing much. Guards literally live and die by their attitude the moment they are forced into action. The best can command high salaries and be entrusted with the lives of the Empire’s most important personalities and most valuable objects. This includes the Cemetery Guards who defend the Gardens of Morr in the dead of night, watching out for potential grave robbers, as well as the Temple Guards, protectors of sacred sites and important priests. Merchants often need local Guards, for valuable goods stored in warehouses or in transit. Some claim that personal bodyguards have the most interesting jobs, because they just have to stay with their prestigious employers, and have a front row seat to watch these important people evolve, right before their eyes. “If you are not on the list, you do not enter! - Anonymous Altdorf Guard to the Grand Theogonist, during the coronation of Karl Franz I, apocryphal Guardsmen can enter the adventure when their function is compromised. Any self-respecting guard would want to track and investigate those who found them wrong, and return what they guarded to their true owners. It can easily turn into an exciting adventure. Many who go on expeditions will need guards to accompany them for profit or to an untimely death."

"You fight for the money, for the glory, and to entertain the crowds. Watching fights is a popular pastime. In the cities, organized fights take place every night. We can become rich on the backs of spectators, and even more by betting on the results. Winners earn money and earn local hero status. The losers are injured or killed. Because pit fighting is officially frowned upon, fights are often controlled by gangs of criminals, but the wealthy like to slum on occasion, especially if it involves a little bloodshed. Tilean Gladiators are the most renowned, though Marienburg’s Chain Fighters and Kislev’s Beastmasters also draw crowds. Pugilists and wrestlers can work in a traveling fair, challenging the audience to survive three minutes in the ring with them, or take on a famous opponent to the cheers of the crowd. Knives, clubs, chains, boxing, wrestling, there is an almost endless variety of styles and codes that a Gladiator can adopt. “Approach! Approach! Do you dare to face the power of Gosser? Could you last three minutes with Resige Heuhaufer? - Raimund Heenan, Arena Barker Many Gladiators come into this profession because they have talent or simply need the money. Some jump at the chance to leave their seedy world behind and put their talent to good use. Luckily, Gladiators are generally free to use their time as they please, as long as they come back on time for the next big fight, and even if they don’t there are always others. pits…"

"Highly talented botanists who benefit from Rhya’s bounty to create remedies for many ailments. Medicines concocted by Apothecaries are prohibitively expensive and rarely available in the Reiklander Hinterlands. This is why peasants regularly turn to the healing power of plants, collected, treated and administered by Herbalists. The transmission of the knowledge of the Herbalists takes place for the most part orally, which means that, very often, the names of the diseases will vary from one village to another. Renowned Herbalists, among the most experienced, are dispatched in the event of mysterious or particularly resistant diseases. Herbalists spend much of their time visiting those who are ill, seeking to diagnose the ailment they are stricken with before seeking out the herbs needed to craft a cure. Some Herbalists practice their profession less honorably and are sought after by those who cannot afford certain expensive illicit substances.
