Although this is a mistaken stereotype, there is a running joke in the profession that Halfling Herbalists are only interested in pipe weed and the root of Destiny. Herbalists very easily find a place in a group of adventurers or mercenaries thanks to their knowledge of poultices and potions. When particularly virulent diseases spread, it often happens that the Supreme Herbalists send their apprentices to search for rare herbs in remote places, and some sometimes find themselves in complicated situations. The wood elves’ expertise in herbalism has become legendary. In the Gray Mountains, the goddess Shallya is said to have traveled to Athel Loren to seek their advice when Ranald succumbed to an illness she was unable to cure. High elves who study herbalism follow the teachings of Lileath the Virgin, and rumor has it that there is an elven library in Marienburg listing the medical uses of all Old World plants, though no humans was again granted access."

Item.name: satchel containing an assortment of herbs

Career.Explanation: "You prey on travellers, extorting a right of way from the most vulnerable and unwary. …and he said, “Titus, why are you taking these shears? And I go, “These?“ And he goes, “Yeah, those are the only shears I see.“ So I laughed and said, “Sometimes they don’t want to give me their rings like I ask them.“ When I show them the shears, they quickly change tack. And if they don’t…” “Ha! Ha! Ah!” - Titus Widmann, Outlaw Outlaws roam the roads of the Old World in search of vulnerable travelers and merchant caravans. They lead dangerous and often miserable lives. Many do not see themselves as criminals, but as a group of oppressed people trying to live their free lives, free from constraints. Many Wood Elf Outlaws fit this description, pushing back the proliferation of Humans to the edges of the forests, ready to take actions far more drastic than their fellows. Particularly cunning and brutal Outlaws can form their own bands, sometimes even uniting multiple bands under one banner. These Bandit Kings are feared and reviled by nobles and peasants alike. Although few Outlaws make the distinction in choosing their prey, some claim to protect the common people. These good Samaritans focus their larceny on the avaricious nobles, and in return the locals provide them with food, information, and safe haven. Not all Outlaw warbands are made up of wild monsters, so many can be reasoned with if approached correctly. A party of adventurers may ask an Outlaw to accompany them as a guide or to protect them, especially if the party is trying to put an end to unholy activity in the domain of a Bandit King. Lone Outlaws may find it easy to join an adventuring party. But they may need to dress up if they are wanted where they are going."

"You create machines and constructs that are as weird as they are useful and often downright deadly. “Master Engineer Volker von Meinkopt found inspiration watching students reloading at the Imperial School of Artillery. He had a revelation: more cannons = more shots = more potential deaths. So he quickly made the first repeating handgun, “Von Meinkopt’s Spinning Death Cavalcade“ as well as the first “Von Meinkopt’s Micro-Spring Pernicious Lead Volleys“ pistol. And since there was no question of him resting on his laurels, he then invented this huge 9-barrel cannon, the Hellfire repeating cannon, a deadly weapon for those in his line of sight and , very often, for the team that handles it. - “Great Engineer of the Empire” Dame Theodora Holzenauer, Engineer and Journalist Engineers are able to design and manufacture devices or mechanical structures such as bridges, canals or even fortifications. Most of them have been trained, the dwarves in the very rigid guild of Dwarf Engineers, the humans in avant-garde establishments such as the Imperial School of Engineers in Altdorf, even if the we also unearth some talented autodidacts. Human Engineers value innovation and discovery, while Dwarfs prefer to rely on designs that have been proven for generations. Mining company engineers are very well paid; those of the Army who maintain the war machines of the Empire and officiate as sappers and builders of bridges, much less. Master Engineers often have to manage entire teams on ambitious construction projects. Chartered Engineers are the most respected in the Empire, commissioned to design, test, and execute Imperial Commands, such as Steam Paddlewheels, which have revolutionized the speed of transport on the canals of Vorbergland. Some Engineers carry out research in Dwarf Fortresses, most of them abandoned, because they contain trade secrets from the old days. Those who dare to venture into the depths of these places sometimes find wonders dating back millennia, many of which have been hijacked by goblins and skaven for their nefarious purposes. The gigantic stone bridges that tower over these fortresses are equally breathtaking, some stretching for miles, veritable wonders and remnants of a bygone era that once connected the cities, forts, and arable farms of the dwarves."

"You guard the territory of others, ensuring that everything is in order, and, if necessary, protected. Stewards are in charge of maintaining their employer’s properties. Failing to beautify - or at least maintain - their land or supply it regularly usually leads to disgrace. In certain circumstances, several Stewards may work together to maintain the lands of the same employer. Stewards only leave their domain if they are compelled to do so by duty. That being said, even those assigned to guard the land of an estate, or a game reserve, must regularly patrol to monitor the general condition of the property and discourage poachers. When they are between two missions, the Intendants find themselves employed as guides or hunters, a source for them of as much excitement as terror. Those who feel resentment for some of their former masters are sometimes even inclined to provide confidential information, relating to the domains of which they were responsible, to the enemies of these latter. The duties of a Steward include many areas: maintaining an imposing estate, overseeing the hunting grounds of a lord or even ensuring that the rarely used holiday home is always in perfect condition. Stewards can also ensure the surveillance of cultivable or wooded areas, or even maintain lakes, rivers and basins. Those who serve the wealthiest and most powerful people have the opportunity to find themselves in very advantageous positions."

"You navigate through a totally unfair legal system, defending your clients and prosecuting the culprits. “It’s not what the lawyer says about my rights that worries me, but more what is reasonable and within the scope of justice. These elements should form the basis of our new law. - Lector Agatha von Böhrn, Supreme Chancellor of the Empire. Lawyers provide legal advice, interpret laws and plead for their clients in court. They are often specialized in the laws of the province in which they practice or in ecclesiastical law. Most have studied in universities and are therefore wealthy and influential, although some gifted individuals of low extraction are sometimes their apprentices. Cult jurists learn from their fellows, and those instructed by the Cults of Verena and Sigmar are especially valued. Some Lawyers are employed as mediators, settling informal disputes outside of expensive courts, one of the halflings’ favorite roles. Others work for gangs of criminals, exploiting legal loopholes to free their still-guilty clients. At the top of the ladder, the Masters of the Bar are the only Lawyers who have the right to plead before the courts of appeals of the city-states and demand exorbitant commissions for their services. Lawyers excel at getting others out of trouble when adventurers excel at getting them into it. They can use their knowledge of certain obscure laws of the region to avoid trouble by suggesting individual approaches to solving difficult problems. After all, it is more profitable, and less dangerous, to take a thug to court than to tie him up in a cellar."

"“If Nuln wants a trade war, so be it. I can see a blockade on their river and an increase in gun taxes. After all, the Empire owes me a few favors…” - Leo van Haagen, Merchant Prince of Marienburg You are smart, you can count perfectly, you buy low and sell high, and you make more money than the most will never see one. The vast majority of Merchants trade in rather simple goods such as alcohol, textiles, pottery or wooden objects. For the more ambitious, some rare and exotic goods, such as dwarven gromril or spices from the East, bring much more, but take much longer to ship and require strong foreign connections. In most cities, Merchants are not allowed to sell without having permission from a Merchant Guild (and paying for it), which are such powerful institutions that they come from to have a political influence similar to that of the nobles of the court. Local trade is managed by Merchants who transport goods between remote villages and the nearest towns. “How did I become a millionaire? Well, when I was just a little girl with just a penny left, I went to a local farmer and bought him an apple. Then I went to the market and sold the apple for two cents. The next day, I bought two apples from the farmer, then I returned to the market where I sold these two apples for four cents. And so on, every day I would go to the farm where I would buy apples before going to the market to resell them and make a profit. And at the age of 25, my grandfather died, bequeathing me a million crowns. - Johanna Sainzburg, Fresh Fruit Magnate Merchants share a certain affinity with adventurers, and often prefer to hire them instead of using trade caravan escorts. Adventurers, bold in nature and able to adapt easily, are ideal candidates for partnerships in trading businesses and thus allow Merchants to come into contact with a host of colorful Characters. Merchants can join a guild by learning from Master Merchants as junior associates. The Merchant Princes, who have warehouses and sales offices in multiple cities, have almost the same status as the lesser nobility. In addition to trade,"

"“Yep, I sailed to Marienburg. Those cursed Wastelanders did everything they could to keep us from taking to the high seas. I swear, the Boatman had to circumnavigate the islands three times before we finally smelled the salt water. And they taxed us double on everything. Even the crew cat got it. Honestly, I’m glad to be home. - Thom Wesserbrug, Boatswain The call of the open sea and a life spent sailing the seas resonate with you, even though many Reikland Sailors have never seen the sea. Sailors sail the high seas in the Navy Imperial, or put themselves at the service of Merchants. Although the Reikland has no coastline, the Reik, between the Wasteland and Altdorf, is several miles wide and used by many large ships. The Imperial First Fleet, which patrols these waters, rarely sees the high seas, largely because the taxes to pay to bring a warship through Marienburg are exorbitant. Once Marienburg has been crossed, the whole world awaits the Sailor: the dangerous Sea of Claws, the Great Ocean of unfathomable depths, the Islands of Mermaids and their exoticism, the South Seas and the Black Gulf. And even on the Reik, a Sailor can spend his entire life traversing its waters without ever experiencing the same day. A Sailor always manages to find work, whether as a crew member on an Empire combat ship or as a simple crew member on a trade sloop. Some Sailors travel the world and pay for their transportation by working. The Reik also has many “Missions“, these buildings provided by the Imperial Navy, and which employ many Sailors."

"With a steady hand and a strong heart, you practice medicine, fighting to save lives. “Beware of the Bronze Doctor. - Reiklander proverb that warns against too approachable doctors. Physicians study the symptoms of their patients and prescribe remedies or perform surgery. While the art of healing is ancient, and largely derived from Elvish practices, the formal science of medicine is relatively new, and many are unconvinced of its efficacy. Due to the Empire’s history with necromancy and the guarantees demanded by the Cult of Morr, the study of corpses is forbidden, making it difficult to learn anatomy. The reputation of medicine is also damaged by scammers who sell miracle cures without any effect, if they do not cause even more suffering to those who use them. Medics learn their profession at a university or study in the Medics Guild. Most inexpensive surgeries are performed by backyard doctors, known as totally unofficially trained barber-surgeons. Doctors with medical degrees and strong hearts are in high demand in the Army. The most famous Doctors practice only with the richest merchants and nobles. “They are bastards, all of them. I can’t even give you a good bloodletting without their permission. “Practice of medicine without a license“, you speak. I know you can’t afford their services, honey. Here, honey, have this tea. What ? Oh no, it’s just tea. And if you feel better, you thank Shallya, huh? - Jana Palner, Part-Time Surgeon It is common knowledge that Physician Guild fees are exorbitant, meaning that sometimes junior Physicians, without an established practice yet, will seek alternative sources of income . Some Doctors are constantly on the lookout for more effective treatments and new drugs, which can take them quite far. Others prefer to perfect their knowledge of anatomy by being the first to study serious injuries, and what better way to do this than to travel with adventurers?"

"You live on the streets and subsist on the charity of others, using your charisma and persuasiveness. “I lost my leg during the Battle of Bögenwasser. I had both hands devoured by a squig when the goblins ambushed us while on patrol near Bögenauser. All to protect the Reikland and our Emperor. - Klaas, Veteran Soldier The rumour, heard mostly in the countryside, that the streets of Altdorf are paved with gold is but a cruel mockery of its Beggars. They can only rely on the generosity of foreigners, and collect the rubbish from the muck of the city, while some braggart dandies do not hesitate to give them, smiling, a few coins to make them clear off. The laws give them little protection, and the guard doesn’t have much sympathy for vagabonds. “You can go to Königsplatz next week - I need you to mess up Luitpoldstrasse today. For what ? Better not ask, all you need to know is the Cutters need the Guard distracted. And, for the sake of my business, I try not to offend the Cutters, and if you want to become successful, I advise you to follow my example. - “The Kaiser”, King of the Beggars of Altdorf The Beggars, mostly orphans, end up in the streets after going back and forth to Houses of Mercy for a good part of their lives. Once they learn the basics of begging and know how to beg a little, Beggars improve their techniques using disguises and other ploys to attract the sympathy of others. Some Beggars, however, are not destitute, but employees of the lowest rungs of the social ladder, such as scavengers, rag pickers, and bone collectors."

"Fast and confident, nothing will prevent you from delivering your message on time. “It sounded like a bundle of value, if you know what I mean. I thought I’d just take a look. Maybe it was for his girlfriend. I thought it might be a little naughty, you know? How could I have guessed it was just spy stuff. By the way, where is Bretonnia? - Rufus Drucht, Messenger who managed to capture the bloody Bretonnian spy ring single-handedly, before losing his job. When the post service proves too long or too risky, people send a Messenger. Many courier companies offer express services, each striving to demonstrate that they are the fastest and most secure. Most Messengers take their craft seriously, protecting their bundle at the risk of their lives. Some Messenger companies have made agreements with relays, providing the Messenger with a fresh horse against his exhausted mount, thus ensuring the shortest possible delays. Messages can contain all kinds of information, and some can lead to various adventures if intercepted. The easiest way for an enemy (or an unaware group) to get their hands on such information is to hijack a Messenger. If this happens, the Messenger will keep following the trail of the message until he recovers it. Messengers usually work on their own account and are paid by the fare. It is therefore easy for them to take a break once a mission is completed and resume when they feel like it again. Runners are tasked with carrying urgent messages through cities. In large cities, competitions are often organized to determine which is the fastest of all. The winners are rewarded with various prizes and highly lucrative missions. Messengers also frequently work for the military, Noble Houses, large Chambers of Commerce or even for certain criminal gangs who want to remain discreet."

"You are the guarantors of peace and you maintain order among the populace so that your city does not descend into anarchy. Minutemen are employed by local authorities to patrol the streets of the Empire. Most are no more than volunteer hired peacekeepers and very few know the laws they are supposed to enforce. Corruption is rampant, and many Minutemen engage with the authorities for the sole purpose of hurting others or aiding local criminal gangs. Some manage to triple their balances by closing their eyes. “I’m sorry, sir, I have a Halfling assassin, a mystracine smuggling ring, a gang war, and a noble threatening to have me arrested by my own Militia. Your missing cat will have to wait until tomorrow. - Sergeant Harri Makkenpieser, Altdorf Militia Not all Militia are dishonest, but those with a certain amount of ethics are quickly disillusioned with the corruption that pollutes the system. By joining groups of adventurers, these Minutemen can uphold justice on their own terms. Street experience makes them highly effective fighters in a small group, and their presence in that group can help legitimize this bunch of no-goods. Only a few towns and cities have professional Militiamen who are paid to understand and uphold the laws. In many cases, the Emperor’s Peace is maintained by the Army, whose men guard the ramparts, the gates and patrol the streets in accordance with the instructions of their superiors."

"It is in the darkest depths of the earth that, day after day, you break stone, backbreaking work if ever there was one. Many Independent Miners sometimes find themselves in a very difficult position when they come across goblins or other underground horrors. Some, however, believe that this life is more lucrative, even if more dangerous, than that of serving a mine owner to earn a living. Many opportunities for adventure present themselves regularly to Prospectors, and sometimes they even form a team together in order to seek fortune and glory. Many Prospectors have heard tales of gold in the Skaag Hills, but mining these dark and dangerous tunnels is very taxing work. The Miners, experts in the manufacture of supports and in the extraction of the veins of ore which they recover for resale, are very vigilant as to the unexpected dangers which could arise due to the gases generated by the greenskins. They are very tough, both physically and mentally. Prospectors usually work on commission, and have a license that allows them to share their discoveries with the local lord. Some fortunes of the nobility were built on the wealth drawn from the mines of their lands, and, very often, the Miners who work in these exploitations are criminals or debtors forced to work there. The quarrymen who carve in stone in the open have a less dangerous job than those who work underground, but accidents remain frequent and the beastmen, likely to attack from the edge of the nearby forests, represent a danger to all. moments. In the eyes of the dwarves, work in the mines is not reserved for commoners. On the contrary, they are considered experts of great talent and are particularly respected among the Dawi. The dwarves, who have an innate sense of stone, possess a kind of flair when it comes to consolidating certain underground passages. Some dwarves are so proud of their expertise in the art of mining that when they go to war, they arm themselves with pickaxes instead of axes."

"You have a talent for seeing the future, or for convincing others that you do... People, who seek answers in this dangerous world, turn to Mystics when they want a glimpse of their future. Traveling caravans of Strigany are commonplace in the Reikland, and many locals will collect as many coins as possible in order to predict good fortune, as well as buy charms and love potions. Mystics are generally shrewd and intuitive, allowing them to guess the cravings and fears of those who come to them and give them just enough answers to be believable. Mystics must be careful, for they walk a fine line between trickery and heretical sorcery. Mystics demonstrate their abilities in many different ways: Palmists and seers are very numerous among the Strigany, but a Wood Elf will rather tend to interpret the different signs and symbols he finds in the surrounding nature or to s inspired by his dreams and other visions. Many cults have their own Prophets and Sages, each predicting the future through the paradigms of their respective beliefs. “I have never met a priest who could predict my future. Well, if we ignore the Priest of Morr who predicted my death for three cents, but don’t they always say that death and taxes are the only certain things in this life? - Sylvestr Jutzenbach, Noble of Ostermark Mystics may find themselves treading the paths of adventure if their visions attract the attention of Priests and Witch Hunters. The dreams and visions of Mystics often allow them to join groups of adventurers. The Mystic may have had a vision of a dark future if nothing is done? Whatever their motivations, once on the road, Mystics always have plenty of opportunities to ply their trade."

"You lure ships and sink them to the bottom before retrieving the cargo. Sometimes the gods will offer a boon to local residents in the form of a ship with a tragic fate. But sometimes the gods need a helping hand: that’s where the Shipwreckers come in. By laying treacherous traps and sending disturbing signals, the Shipwreckers manage to lure unwary navigators to shoals sand or rocks before recovering what is in the wreckage, without worrying about the protests of possible survivors of the crew. “If we let the crew live, they will tell the patrol boats where we are operating, so the only reasonable thing to do is to kill them all. - Mandel Stein, Pragmatic River Pirate Preparing for and executing a shipwreck is an adventure in itself: avoiding authorities, disposing of assets, making sure everyone holds their tongues, and spending the agent so earned, all of which provide opportunities for danger and adventure. And how do you know what cargo will be discovered, and who will come and hunt them down once the theft has taken place? The Shipwreckers, whose daily life is made up of these adventures, will have no trouble leaving this existence and returning to it when the time comes again. Some Shipwreckers are particularly proud of their clever traps, which manage to give the illusion of an accident when sinking and allow them to stay at a respectable distance. Some board ships and toss the crew overboard, able to spot ships with heavy cargoes and the weakest defenses at a glance. These River Pirates are hunted by both the Road Patrolmen and the rivers and are constantly on the move in order to escape the authorities."

Item.name: flotilla of river transport boats with a crew of Shipwreckers

Career.Explanation: "You pilot some of the most treacherous waters of the Old World. Les Nautoniers are specialized river guides who know the region’s rivers inside out. They are very numerous near the most dangerous stretches of rivers in the Empire and do not hesitate to ask for large sums to accomplish a mission, even if some think the task is rather easy. Others feel that it is a cheap price compared to a lost cargo. Nautoniers, experts in their field, are often hired by wealthy clients who need a specialist in the field when they embark on voyages to unknown lands. Even when crossing waters they do not know, the Nautoniers are very useful, because their knowledge of rivers and piloting is irreplaceable. As their work is mainly seasonal, they will not hesitate to drop everything to go wherever they want. This freedom corresponds perfectly to the lifestyle of adventurers, and makes it just as easy to return to the job of Nautier if the adventures experienced have not made it possible to meet their needs. Most Boaters will stick to a single famous stretch of river, while others will make the most profit during the time of year when the waters are most dangerous. Other Nautoniers, familiar with more waterways, will guide the ships throughout their crossing, then taking on the role of navigator. This is often the case for merchant ships carrying valuable cargo at the worst times of the year."

"As a scion of noble lineage, you strut proudly above the rabble. The blood of high-line ancestors runs through the veins of the nobility, granting them the right to rule, enact laws, and dispense justice. Nobles generally inherit immense estates and considerable fortune, although only direct descendants can claim to wield any power. Many people spend their lives maintaining this wealth and the power they wield through politics, conquest and business. Those with no significant heritage must forge their own path in the world, joining the Army, or the Navy, as a commanding officer, or else serving a god. It frequently happens that Nobles ally themselves with other, more important houses, for example by sending their daughters to work there as bridesmaids for members of the royal family. Many Nobles serve their families while away from home in hopes of improving their circumstances and receiving praise from their peers. Others, tired of this idle existence, will seek the thrill in a life of adventurer and pseudo hero. Heirs whose prospects are blocked sometimes leave to seek their fortune far from the intrigues and betrayals of the court and engage in various activities allowing them to widen their field of possibilities. The GM must think carefully before allowing one of his Players to choose the Noble Career. The latter makes it possible to possess many goods and to exercise a certain power, especially in the last levels of Career."

"You are at the service of your divinity, having taken a vow of a pious life. Nuns are part of religious orders and are normally cloistered within an abbey, a convent or a monastery. Most rise before sunrise to perform their Morning Prayers before doing their labor in the fields, caring for the sick, or working to preserve important manuscripts. Pilgrimage oaths compel some to travel across the Empire while others have vowed to aid the community, walking alongside the people and ministering to their spiritual needs. Some hermits, like those who tend shrines, are often called Nuns or Monks by the inhabitants of the Empire. Many nuns learn the essential trades of winegrowers, brewers or cartographers. The Abbesses promote these activities in order to attract donations from the local nobility. Leaders of military orders, or very unifying, enjoy significant influence within their own cult as well as with the ruling class of a province. To learn more about the different religions and the different orders, refer to Chapter 7: Religions and Beliefs. “ Quickly ! Hurry up ! The Sisters of Faith and Chastity will march through the streets. I’m curious to see if I manage to wedge a few copper coins between their spines. It brings good luck for a whole year! - Bengt, Wanderer of Altdorf When a religious order discovers terrible secrets or part of a prophecy, its leaders often feel the need to act by sending brothers and sisters out into the world. The abbeys along the pilgrimage routes will regularly send their members to protect the many pilgrims who travel the long sacred roads of the Empire. Likewise, there will always be itinerant religious traveling the world and going on an adventure in each new territory they discover."

"Tireless and sure of yourself, you patrol the rivers relentlessly, chasing down outlaws and troublemakers. “There was a time when I was a River Patrolman and Big Willi came to me so that I wouldn’t take on some cargo. He told me that the only thing I had to do was let him pass and everything would be fine. I was young then. So, I told everything to the owner of the boat. Have I been thanked for my honesty? Nah, Big Willi showed up, beat me up, and the next day I got kicked out of the Patrollers. They were all in cahoots, huh? - Nikki Schnelling, ex-River Patrolman The sound of a bugle on a river heralds the arrival of the Imperial River Patrol, an armed task force as renowned for its brutes as it is for its efficiency. Most of the inns and riverside villages keep a place for them at anchor, because, without their presence, the waters would remain under the control of dangerous criminals. These overworked patrols focus on the most horrific crimes, and settle for solving minor offenses with one-off fines. On the main trade routes, they have larger ships manned by Boarders trained to fend off larger threats, such as greenskins or trolls. A conscientious River Patroller, who searches the buildings and who pushes his research further, risks at any moment to come across something unclear or on a sinister cargo. Generally, they work a month in a row before resting for a full month. This type of schedule is ideal for going on an adventure, especially since the River Patroller does not have to desert if he has decided to do something else, or even waste time trying to convince his Sergeant that it is his duty to investigate the crimes. They can therefore step back, investigate on their own and resume their post before the start of the next cycle. Some River Patrollers rarely put their boots on a boat, supervising outposts that control strategically important waters. Others patrol on fast ships and are responsible for intercepting smugglers operating at night. The largest ships of the River Patrollers are veritable warships bristling with cannons and mortars, ready for any eventuality."

"With your eyes always on the lookout and your hand on the hilt of your weapon, you travel the great roads of the Empire enforcing the law. “So I was stopped by a Patrol the other day. She told me to watch out for an unscrupulous fellow who prowls the roads and asks unfortunate travelers for three sous to let them pass. I thanked her for her valuable advice. “Let Taal guide you,” she replied, “that will be three cents. - Ullrich the Peddler Highway Patrollers protect travelers from bandits, greenskins, beastmen, and other perils that lurk along the main highways of the Empire. Patrollers are paid through a system of customs taxes that they mostly collect on their own. The most recognized Highway Patrollers are highly respected and welcomed. They are often reserved a berth in the inns they encounter along the roads. A large majority of Highway Patrollers, part of the Imperial Army, roam the most important thoroughfares in peacetime, fully trained and impressive in their impeccable uniforms. The roads less traveled must be satisfied with the Patrolmen of the region, and it happens that some take advantage of their status and abandon surveillance to carry out more remunerative tasks. Some Patrollers will prefer to stay in their fortified guard posts rather than going to watch the roads. But travelers will be reluctant to donate money if the roads are poorly maintained and dangerous. Road Patrollers have no difficulty finding something to go on an adventure. When an unfortunate event occurs, it is often close to a well-guarded road. When problems arise, Highway Patrollers are called in to sort things out. If they answer the call and undertake research, they are just doing their job, earning a few extra coins for their trouble, even if the ensuing adventure takes them far from their usual sector."

"Trafficking in bodies and limbs is lucrative, with high demand from universities and doctors for fresh corpses. Besides the scientific market, bodies are sometimes buried along with all sorts of valuables under the grave markers of the tombs in the Gardens of Morr. Because their work is obviously illegal and sacrilegious, Grave Robbers generally operate under the guise of darkness. The Body Dealers are said to cut out the middleman and pick beggars and other unfortunates straight from the streets. Grave robbers avoid the legal risks of looting the recently dead, and instead go to ruins and ancient burial mounds, risking encountering the restless dead and brigands there. Strangely, some victorious Treasure Hunters are hailed as heroes, their treasures sold to the aristocracy who then display them. It is even said that the great fortune of one of the orders of chivalry came from several of its members who had plundered a foreign tomb. “Khemri’s nightmares still haunt me. The curses cast by these long-dead tyrants have sealed my fate. I can only hope that Morr can end the necromancy that rots my bones and blackens my heart. - Lady Estelle Hauptleiter, Treasure Hunter (deceased) Grave robbers easily embrace a life of adventure, especially if their nocturnal sojourns are discovered by unsympathetic authorities. They may also be called upon by antique dealers who wish to engage their specialized services in the excavation of a tomb, or perhaps they will feel compelled to track down a necromancer suspected of using bodies for abominable purposes."

"You carry the word of your god and satisfy the spiritual needs of the masses. “The priestess of Shallya, just a kid, put her hand on my little Anton’s forehead while whispering and he immediately stopped screaming. He smiled at me for the first time in days. I’ll never forget. Oh, he died a few days later, but he didn’t suffer. No, he did not suffer. - Sabine Schmidt, Fishmonger The Priests take care of all the faithful in the Old World. Although most are assigned to specific temples, others prefer a life of wandering in order to reach devotees who cannot, or do not want to visit the temples. They are expected to embody the beliefs of their religion - which will depend on the deity they serve. High Priests are responsible for a temple, and all of its worshipers and laity. They are often called upon, alongside the Lectors, to advise the ruling classes, and many are those who play an active role in the politics of a region. The Priests have many obligations relating to their god, such as the duty of consecration of the new ships of the Priests of Manann or the responsibility of those of Shallya towards the sick and wounded. They are therefore involved in all aspects of the life of the Empire. To learn more about religion and the different orders, see Chapter 7: Religions and Beliefs. “Look, there’s nothing to worry about. The Night of the Witches, the Hexensnacht takes place every year. We just have to ask the Lord of Death to watch over us. And, when midnight strikes, we will call MORR! MORR! MORR! - Father Wilhelm Abgott, Priest of Morr Some Priests, who normally must serve in temples, seek excuses to sojourn outside. When they hear of strange problems reported by their congregation, they can go in search of answers. Some High Priests find the administrative obligations so far removed from what they imagined when they joined the cult that they go on long pilgrimages away from their temple."

"You summon the divine into the thick of battle, slaying the enemies of the Empire in righteous fury. Some cults of the Empire have clerics trained for war. In the Reikland, the Warrior Priests of Sigmar are the most common example, and many of the Empire’s armies are accompanied by priests carrying hammers and encouraging soldiers in the name of Sigmar. But other cults, especially those of Myrmidia, Ulric, Taal and Morr have their own Warrior Priests, each with their own unique views on how a war should be fought. Off the battlefield, Warrior Priests are also expected to care for the spiritual well-being of soldiers, ensuring that their motivation remains intact and discipline is upheld. Certain orders of Warrior priests take an oath to roam the Empire, unearthing heresy wherever it is found, helping where they can. Others prefer not to join the armies, but to lead them... Although many Warrior Priests remain in the army, some serve their worship through missionary work, and others roam the Empire as they please. As such, Warrior Priests are born adventurers. Of course, to pursue their goals to the far reaches of the Empire, they may need permission from their cult, and perhaps their commanders."

"You are a member of an organized criminal gang, collecting debts and extorting money from the weak. “IF YOU CAN’T PAY THE PRICE, DON’T MAKE THE BET. - Bosco’s Bones Listing (Altdorf Gambling) The Ransomers extort money from law-abiding citizens and merchants, providing “protection“ or similar fraudulent “service“. If the “fees” are not paid on time, the victims, their families and their livelihoods are at considerable risk. Major gangs bribe or intimidate local authorities into ignoring their activities - their cutthroats are always ready to kill - or worse - to keep their business running smoothly. Cutthroats are employed to collect debts of all kinds, especially those resulting from lost bets or high-interest loans. In a world plagued by poverty, the promise of easy wealth is an allure that many fools are unable to ignore. The more organized corruption is, the larger and more complex the organizations running them. While the smallest deals are run by small gangs confined to a building or two, larger ones can span cities and even entire regions, and the crime lords who run them can wield extraordinary power. “Or bosco will break your legs. - Addition scribbled in chalk below Bosco’s Bones inscription Cutthroats and Ransomers are always ready to use threats and violence, making them useful members of many groups wishing to face a aggressive opposition. Gang Leaders can even run their business on the road, trying to expand their territory or explore new opportunities for lucrative plots. Given the competitive nature of some trafficking, even the most powerful crime lords can be dethroned by adversaries, or through treachery. Forced into hiding or fleeing, some mobsters may seek to use a group of experienced adventurers to their own advantage."

"You prevent civilization from being invaded by vermin with the help of your faithful canine companions. “ Sorry my friend. The rest of the guild takes care of the rats. My friends and I take care of the bigger stuff in the sewers. There are loads of them down there...“ - Mårten Stormdal, Exterminator of Ubersreik Ratters patrol every town and city, and for good reason. The streets of the Empire are overflowing with stinking trash of various foods, the perfect breeding ground for vermin. The Ratters make their living killing these rats, clearing the basements of their nests, and plunging into the heart of the Empire’s sewers, which are literally infested with them...provided they are brave enough to face the other creatures there. swarm. At the beginning of their training, most Ratters adopt a puppy that they train to hunt rats. The Ratters are hired by the cities and become Sewers who go hunting for giant rats and other underground nuisances. Sometimes entire towns are overrun by rats, in which case they call in Exterminators. The Ratters change towns when the rats become “too big“ or “too smart“, or when the competition is too fierce. When traveling, they may befriend those who accept the help of a street slinger, especially since ratters are willing to venture where others refuse to go. If you want to play a Character who knows what those “too big” or “too smart” Skaven are (see page 336), the Ratter is for you. However, Skaven have a habit of murdering those who spread rumors about them. Because of this, the wisest Ratters will generally not share what they know, with some even going so far as to rely on their professional experience to discredit such “big rats“ or “ratmen“ stories."

Item.name: poison bait bag (10 doses of Heartbreaker)

Career.Explanation: "A savvy expert on valuables, you’ll buy everything, legal or not, and turn it around to pick up a handsome profit. “Why do they call me Receleur? Well ’cause I’m harboring tricks to keep you from getting caught, right. So you fly, and I make sure you don’t have to worry about how to dispose of the goods. Consider me your accomplice. - “Boil“ Vakram, Fence A Fence buys loot from Rogues and resells it for profit, often to those unaware that the goods are being stolen. Brilliant Fences sometimes work as pawnbrokers, importers, and other merchants. Others prefer to remain itinerant, dealing only in transportable objects. Although the average Fence resells goods and valuables, there are also knowledgeable specialists who focus on forbidden information and knowledge. Some Fences move stolen items across the Empire. A painting stolen in Altdorf is easier to sell in Talabheim to customers unaware of the burglary. When prestigious objects disappear, the Receivers are also the first to be consulted by those who seek to acquire them. Some Fencers even take commissions from their clients, for putting them in contact with those who can steal on demand. The search for buyers and sellers, or the need to escape a terrible situation, can take a Fencer far. They can be found all over the Empire and in many regions beyond the borders. Up-and-coming Brocaners transport illicit goods between Old World cities in search of buyers. Others, seeking to make a name for themselves elsewhere, try to make a place for themselves in the existing underground cities. Since their interests are often common, Fencers and Merchants sometimes team up. But with all this criminal activity and all this travelling, trouble is bound to be."

"You hunt the illegal witches infesting the Empire using any means necessary. “If you are not a witch, you have nothing to fear. - Walter Keller, Veteran Witch Hunter, the night before the Almshof fire Few people are as feared and respected as Witch Hunters, who have incredible leeway to carry out their duty. Usually equipped with silver blades and a pair of pistols - difficult indeed to dispel the lead - they pursue their hunts in the most remote corners of the Old World, ready to judge any witch they come across or anyone who dares to host. Most Witch Hunters in the Empire belong to the Cult of Sigmar. The most profane among them are sometimes hired by provincial governments and are nothing more or less than specialized bounty hunters. The Colleges of Magic have their own Witch Hunters they call Guardians of the Magisters who hunt down lone wizards, necromancers and demonologists and they think it is wiser to send a wizard to catch a wizard. The existence of a Witch Hunter is a permanent adventure during which he will travel up and down many provinces. They are called upon whenever signs of unofficial magical manifestations appear, and they are expected to follow them to the source. The higher the reputation of a Witch Hunter, the more he finds himself confronted with dangerous enemies who make him live animated adventures. If you play as a Witch Hunter, take care to ensure that no other Player is playing a Village Sorcerer or Dissident Sorcerer, as this could cause immediate conflict within the party."

"Whether you are high or low extraction, you entertain people to make them forget the harsh reality of life. Acrobats are found all over the Old World, and many roam the roads of Reikland, seeking to earn a living. Some remain assigned to a single theater, others perform alone and still others belong to a troupe. The poorest are no more than itinerant beggars, while the praises of those who perform at the courts of earls and other princes will be sung. It’s not an easy life and people have little pity for bad performances, and won’t hesitate to kick out bad performers after throwing rotten vegetables in their faces. “How do you join the troupe of the Luitpold Theater? By training! - A popular joke in Altdorf “Vladimira Tchaukofiev, a musical prodigy, performed in all the courts of the Empire, performing her compositions for the rich and powerful. Upon her triumphant return to her native Kislev, during the reign of Katerin the Bloody, she premiered her opera The Vampire Counts of Stirland, inspired by her travels in Sylvania. Unconventional, she always leads with a silver wand. - “Advocacy Against Necromancy”, Patriarch Felip Iyrtu, 2415 CI, from Freshman Year Reading List, Amethyst College The most common Acrobats are crowd entertainers, such as jesters, singers, actors, musicians, acrobats, dancers and jugglers, although in the Old World there are much stranger sights as well. The road as far as the eye can see, a new village every night, the smell of paint and the roar of the crowd - life itself is an adventure for a Acrobat who brings joy and excitement to the sad lives of those he entertains . Given their existence on the fringes of respectable society, Acrobats who are a little curious about their surroundings will have many opportunities to go on an adventure."

Item.name: choice of texts (that you don’t know how to read yet)

Career.Explanation: "You are at the service of the powerful, and perform all kinds of tasks for them. “I really don’t know why she keeps wanting to take that damn cat. Between her wardrobe, her travel library and her damn collection of butterflies, I don’t know where to turn! And when it gets lost—because it will, you know—she’s going to want me to find her a new one. Sigmar! Where will I find a baby leopard in Ubersreik? - Reynald, Valet of Dame Kirstin Gottlieb Most people in the service of the nobility are of peasant extraction and happy to be able to escape this industrious mass toiling in the fields. They are taught to cook, clean, serve and take care of the stables. They are provided with room, board, and a salary, but a Servitor’s quality of life will largely depend on how they are treated. Some of them dress their masters, cook or serve meals, manage stocks of wine and other provisions, or take care of green spaces. A Servant can be requisitioned to accompany his employer when the latter goes to his summer residence or when traveling to a large city. These are opportunities that will allow him to go on adventures through the Empire. Young idle heirs, overprotected by their parents, sometimes befriend their young Servants and even go so far as to provide them with adventures, living these vicariously when their servants return and tell them their stories. high deeds. Certain privileged Servers are sometimes entrusted with responsibilities that go beyond their prerogatives, or are loaned to other family members or other peers. More experienced Servants can claim to become Valets, or even Stewards, and then manage the day-to-day affairs of their employer and supervise other Servants. Those in the direct service of royalty are often drawn from the nobility rather than the peasantry."

"You are paid to train, be disciplined and, when necessary, go to war. “Though Lords and Ladies come and go, The life of a soldier, I know only that, Karl Franz commands, and we obey, Over the hills and far beyond. - Marche, 118th Reikland Infantry Regiment, “the Greenbacks”. By order of Emperor Magnus the Pious, since the Great War against Chaos, all provinces of the Empire must maintain a standing State Army. Soldiers are the keystone of these armies, trained to fight together, and whose individual skills are complemented by strength in numbers. Rarely encouraged to think for themselves, Soldiers are known for their deadpan fatalism when ordered to roam over hill and dale in the service of their superiors. Soldiers can be archers, crossbowmen, halberdiers, arquebusiers, swordsmen, or spearmen, and these are just a few typical state regiments. Dwarves recruit Soldiers as sledgehammers and arquebusiers, while Elven troops are usually made up of archers and spearmen. There are many other Soldiers, such as mercenaries, local militiamen (who are rarely better than Recruits), private armies, cult armed forces, etc. Soldiers have little free time, but always have opportunities for adventure. Outside the campaign season, many enjoy extended holidays. Officers in the State Armies can also command small groups of Soldiers to investigate unusual occurrences in their regiment’s “territory“, and some officers see such adventures as a great way to keep their Soldiers in shape. . Non-human Soldiers will often be on missions in the Empire, so adventures by their very nature."

"Rightful holder of a magic as powerful as it is dangerous, you are feared by the citizens of the Empire in whom you inspire the greatest mistrust. Many Magisters leave their College of Magic in debt for courses received. These Sorcerers quickly seek employment or seek fortune on land, sea, or any other place where they are likely to unearth relics, artifacts, and ancient books brimming with magical lore. The nomadic Magisters, eager to prove themselves, are then actively encouraged to test their Skills across the Empire by hunting down any potential danger that threatens the local populations. Sorcerers concentrate one of the eight Winds of Magic, which only spellcasters are able to perceive, in order to cast powerful spells. To be eligible to use magic within the Empire, a human must follow the Articles of Imperial Ordinance and belong to one of Altdorf’s eight Colleges of Magic - each specializing in one of the Winds. , as Magisters can only concentrate one Wind without risking danger. After passing their exams, Novice Sorcerers become Magisters. They study and practice their art with the greatest care, an art which, according to the Articles, they can use outside the colleges only to defend their life, or against the enemies of the Empire. Many Magisters are attached to the Imperial Army, and though they are viewed with great suspicion, no one questions their effectiveness on the battlefield. Sorcerers make great Characters because they add firepower to a party, but they can be tricky for newer Players in that they need to learn additional rules for Spells. For this reason, the GM should keep in mind that he may need to accompany the Sorcerer in order for him to use these rules effectively and provide an advantage to the party. You choose the color of the magic you study when you get the Arcane Magic Talent. To learn more about magic, see Chapter 8: Magic."

"Wisdom and shrouded in an aura of mystery, you guide your community with an ancient magic passed down from generation to generation. A Village Sorcerer is often the first to notice suspicious supernatural manifestations. The ensuing search regularly leads them to all sorts of dangerous adventures. When a Witch Hunter arrives in town, village Sorcerers tend to leave, laying low or going on a journey until all danger has passed. Witch Hunters use the term “village sorcerer“ to refer to anyone who uses magic illegally, but that hasn’t always been the case. In the past, Village Sorcerers were highly respected members of rural communities and practiced magic even older than the forests. But decades of persecution, spawned by the emergence of the Colleges of Magic, have reduced their numbers to a few survivors, scattered across the world and utterly broken. They now hide in the quieter places of the Old World, in their smoking huts and creaking hovels on the border between civilized areas and wilderness. Most Village Sorcerers have decided to live solitary in order to protect themselves from unwanted visitors. But their talents are known to all the locals. They keep to themselves the secrets allowing them to protect themselves from evil, but very often they are asked to benefit from their knowledge of herbalism, or to help with childbirth, or even to receive treatment. These Sorcerers are known by many names across the Empire, yet they are united in one goal: to prevent the disappearance of their ancient traditions. Village Sorcerers do not hold the Colleges of Magic close to their hearts, for they know full well that any child taken from them will never return and furthermore will be conscripted into a distant war. When possible, they hide the children they consider “blessed“ so that they never become minions of the Colleges, although sometimes one of them will be sent - spy or sacrifice, who knows? ?"

"Willing and ambitious, you strive to master magic without an official license. Dissenting Wizards lead dangerous lives. Although some present themselves as official Sorcerers, such deceptions are easily discernible to anyone familiar with magic. However, groups of adventurers - especially those without unwavering faith or moral scruples - rarely bother with the precise aspects of a Sorcerer’s education as long as the methods used are effective and not associated with the Dark Gods. . Although unauthorized sorcery is illegal - punishable by death - many Magisters have brief experience as a Dissident Sorcerer before entering the Colleges of Magic. This fact is recognized by the Colleges and Cults, so a dissenting Sorcerer, if discovered, should submit to the authorities. Training in the Colleges can take place between two adventures, which means that a Dissenting Sorcerer can later return to a Sorcerer’s Career (recognized by the Colleges), or become the focus of a new adventure. Anyone with the rare skill of wielding magic must, by law, be trained by the Magisters of the Colleges of Magic. Not everyone accepts such a fate; some people hide their powers or run away. These people are dissident Wizards. They risk madness and damnation, for magic consumes them through lack of proper training, and they seldom understand the nature of the forces they cobble together. Others fully embrace their burgeoning powers, accepting the risk. There are Dissenting Sorcerers of all kinds, for the talent to wield magic comes in many ways without any particular inclination. Some have benevolent personalities and simply love freedom. Others are nobles refusing the idea of being dissident Wizards, because they risk being disinherited. Still others are terrified of what they may become, and so run away. Either way, few will admit what they are, for all are at risk of being burned alive by overzealous Sigmarites."

"A tough guy to hire, to intimidate, fight and maybe even kill for money. “Yeah, Big Yuri came and destroyed all my merchandise. They said this town was just big enough for a lotus smuggler, period. I was fine with it, so I doubled his pay and sent him back to White Tiger’s lair. And it ended like that. - Toni Miragliano, Lotus Trader Swordsmen live on their wits and brawn and are generally not fussy about the kind of work they do. A merchant may want to scare his rival. An employer may decide that their employees need a little encouragement to finish a job faster. A noble may want to scare away his daughter’s suitor. The Swordsmen are then the people they turn to. Those with the worst reputation get the best jobs. A Swordsman can be the bully of a local tavern, and everyone knows he will strike for money, or he is known for his unwavering violence. Some Swordsmen have their own code of conduct, but others only care about money. Some are just bullies who just pick fights and fight with potential targets to see if they can squeeze some money out of the situation. At first glance, Swordsmen are always ready for adventure because they are always ready to fight. But they generally expect to be paid for services rendered. Joining a group without a payment guarantee is something they will need to think about. Could a hardened Swordsman find a cause he would willingly pursue? Maybe he could even make a fresh start?"

"You are rage and dishonor incarnate, seeking a dignified death to regain your lost honor. “Herwig meant no harm, I say! He just asked why the Dwarf had those weird tattoos. It happened so fast, I didn’t even see the dwarf move, just Herwig hit the ground. - Regimius, Longshoreman When dwarves suffer unacceptable humiliation and lose their honor, they take the Slayer’s Oath and follow the path of Grimnir, their ancestral god of warriors. Covering their bodies with tattoos, shaving the sides of their heads, dyeing the remaining hair bright orange, and combing it into spikes with animal fat, they rush through the world, ax in hand, seeking of a glorious death. “We are all going to die, little man. It’s how it happens that counts. - Gotrek Gurnisson, Slayer Slayers roam the Old World in search of dangerous beasts, such as trolls, giants, and dragons. Because of the shame they endure, many suffer depression, gorging themselves on food, alcohol, or stronger stimulants. The more enemies the Slayers face and survive, the more dangerous and crazed they become, gradually seeking out even more dangerous creatures in hopes of finding something to kill them. Until he falls in battle, a Slayer’s life is an adventure. They are on the lookout for opportunities to take on powerful enemies in combat. Slayers will occasionally take up other jobs, to drink their money or pay for their journeys, but they will seek death along the way. All Slayers previously had a life and a Career, so they are much more than mere warriors possessed by their desire to end this. Playing a Killer is a unique experience, because your Character wants to die. Accept it. Look for a terrible destiny. Redeem your honor. Die with dignity."

"You are the heart of rural life and work the land to feed the people. The very fertile Empire of Sigmar abounds in crops, livestock, and a whole host of other easily tradable goods. That is why there is always a lot of work to be done on these lands. Villagers make up the vast majority of the Empire’s population and hold many important roles, including those of farmers, coal miners, woodcutters, millers, shepherds, and many more. Most Villagers depend on the domain of a noble family, where the administration of daily tasks is carried out by a Bailli. The affairs of the village are most often managed by a council, composed equally of farmers and merchants and headed by a Dean. An Alderman or Dean can wield considerable local influence by overseeing many decisions affecting the surrounding lands. “Look, you can laugh in my face all you want, but Konrad the Self-Taught Hero is from the same village as me. So stop talking about us like that, will you? We are good people! - Erika Bauer, farmer The bucolic calm of a protected village is often, for the youngest Villagers, a synonym of the deepest boredom, those who constantly listen to legends speaking of distant lands. Of course, the stories they hear from peddlers or Strigany that only fuel their desire for freedom have little to do with the harsh reality of life in the Empire. During the winter, when food is scarce and the fields do not need tending, young people venture out to the nearest towns and cities in search of work. Sometimes they never come back, unable to do without the excitement of these big cities."

Item.name: tools of the profession (identical to the Profession)

Career.Explanation: "You steal from others in order to line your own pockets, and you’re pretty good at it. “ What is… ? They’re not dogs… they’re bears! - Marx the Mutilated, Unlucky Thief Thieves steal all kinds of wealth and goods from their fellow men. From the humblest pickpocket to the most cunning burglar, the idea of an honest day’s work in exchange for a respectable wage is nothing more than a bad joke. Thieves often organize themselves into gangs with Charlatans, Ransomers and Fences to enrich themselves. The bitter feuds between these illicit organizations are said to last for years, or even decades. The lowliest Rogues target individuals, pickpocketing them or stalking their victims in rat-infested alleys. Burglars avoid confrontation by breaking into businesses and residences, taking portable valuables. The most ambitious Thieves study their targets for days or even weeks, even going so far as to infiltrate the target establishments to gain a better understanding of the layout of the premises. Working with other professional Burglars, such experts can stage heists that their lesser peers can only dream of. “No, the list of charges does not include ’Stealing the Judge’s Heart’. You must be confusing me with a judge with a heart. - Leonora Nithardt, Judge Rogues in trouble with the law are forced to hide or flee, with more and more potential inmates on the loose. Sometimes the items stolen by the Thieves are of exorbitant value or supernatural quality that seem to attract trouble like a rotting body attracts flies. Which can lead to all kinds of unexpected adventures. Of course, a Burglar’s talents are always useful to adventurers, and reliable individuals can expect to be well compensated for their skills."

BonusMalus.Explanation: "Wrap weapons usually have long chains with weights on the end, making them very difficult to parry effectively. Melee Tests against an attack from a Winding weapon suffer a -1 DR penalty, as parried strikes wind around the top of shields or around blades."

"Gunfire followed by billowing smoke and confusion can be terrifying. If you are targeted by a Black Powder weapon, you must pass an Accessible (+20) Calm Test or gain a Broken State, even if the shot misses. Ranged weapons are difficult to master. You cannot attempt a Projectile Test for a weapon for which you do not have the correct specialization. So, if you have Projectiles (Black Powder), you cannot attempt a Projectiles (Bow) Test. There are, however, a few exceptions."
"Your weapon contains Clue ammo, automatically reloaded after each shot you fire. When you have used all your ammo, you must fully reload the weapon using the normal rules."

"Stun weapons are particularly effective at forcing enemies into submission. If you hit the Head with a Stun weapon, attempt an opposed Strength/Resistance Test against the hit target. If you win the Test, your opponent gains a Stunned State."
"All Engineering weapons can be used by Characters with Projectiles (Black Powder), but the weapons lose all their Advantages while keeping their Faults."
BonusMalus.Short: "possible if projectile (black powder) but without bonus"

BonusMalus.Explanation: "Crossbows and Throwing weapons are relatively simple to use. You can attempt a Projectiles (Crossbow) or Projectiles (Throw) Test using your Shooting Skill, but the weapon loses all its Advantages while keeping its Faults."

"Crossbows and Throwing weapons are relatively simple to use. You can attempt a Projectiles (Crossbow) or Projectiles (Throw) Test using your Shooting Skill, but the weapon loses all its Advantages while keeping its Faults."
"Defensive weapons are designed to parry attacks. If you use such a weapon, you gain a +1 DR bonus to any Close Combat Test when you oppose an attack."

"Disruptive weapons can be used to force an opponent back due to their dangerousness or winding ability. Instead of causing Damage, a successful attack with a Disruptive weapon can force an opponent to retreat one meter per DR obtained on the opposite Test."
BonusMalus.Short: "possible to replace a successful test by repelling"

BonusMalus.Explanation: "A Devastating weapon can use the higher of the units die roll or DR to determine the Damage caused by a successful hit. For example, if you roll 34 on your Attack Test and the target number was 52, you can choose to use the DR, which in this case is 2, or the units die roll, which is 4. A Harmless weapon can never be Devastating (Harmless takes precedence)."

"Some weapons are designed to trap other weapons, and sometimes even break them. If you roll a Critical when defending against an attack from a bladed weapon, you can choose to snare it rather than deal a Critical Hit. If you choose this, make an opposed Strength Test, adding your DR obtained from the previous Close Combat Test. If you win, your opponent drops the blade that is ripped from them. If you get a Stunning Success, you not only disarm your opponent, but the force of your maneuver shatters the blade unless it has the Unbreakable Perk. If you fail the Test, your opponent releases his blade and can fight normally."
BonusMalus.Short: "if critical possibility of blocking on strength test"

BonusMalus.Explanation: "Impaling weapons can kill with a single clean strike and cause a Critical Hit on any number divisible by 10 (eg: 10, 20, 30, etc.), as well as a double (eg: 11, 22, 33) rolled less than or equal to the appropriate Combat Test. If the impale is from a ranged weapon, the ammunition used has become firmly lodged in the target’s body. Arrows and bolts require an Intermediate Healing Test to remove – bullets require a surgeon (see the Surgery Talent in Chapter 4: Skills and Talents). Each arrow or bullet not removed prevents you from healing 1 of your Wounds."
"You can use this weapon to attack in Close Combat."
"It is easy to hit your target with this weapon. Gain a +1 DR bonus to any successful Test when attacking with this weapon."
"All Characters within Index meters of the hit target point suffer DR + Weapon Damage and gain all States inflicted by the weapon."
"The weapon is precise and allows easy hitting. Gain a +10 bonus to any Test when using this weapon."

"Your weapon wraps around your opponents, hampering them. Any opponent successfully hit by your weapon gains an Entangled State with Strength equal to your Strength Characteristic. When you Hinder an opponent, you also cannot use the weapon to hit. You can end it whenever you want."
BonusMalus.Short: "opponent must pass a strength test to break free"

BonusMalus.Explanation: "If you use this weapon to oppose an attack, you are considered to have AP Rating in all parts of your body. If your weapon has a Protective Index of 2 or more (thus: Protective 2 or Protective 3), you can also oppose projectiles fired in your Line of Sight."
"The weapon is extremely well designed or made of a particularly resistant material. Under almost all circumstances, this weapon will not be broken, corroded, or dull."

"Rapid weapons are designed to strike with such speed that parrying is not an option, leaving an opponent transfixed before they can react. The wielder of a Rapid weapon can choose to attack with the Rapid weapon outside of the normal Initiative order, whether to strike first, last, or whenever desired. In addition, all Close Combat Tests to defend against Quick weapons suffer a -10 penalty if your opponent uses a weapon without the Quick Edge; other Skills defend normally. Two opponents with Quick weapons fight in Initiative order (relative to each other) as normal. A Fast weapon can never be so Slow (Slow takes over)"

"Some weapons are truly colossal or cause terrible damage due to their weight or design. On a successful hit, add the die result of the units in the attack roll to any Damage caused by a Percussive weapon. A Harmless weapon can never also be Percussive (Harmless takes precedence). ."
"The weapon is extremely effective at penetrating armor. Non-metal APs are ignored, and the first point of all other armor is ignored."
BonusMalus.Short: "Armor opposing 0 if not metal and -1 if metal"

BonusMalus.Explanation: "The weapon takes a long time to reload. A discharged weapon with this defect requires an Extended Projectile Test appropriate to the corresponding Weapon Group and also requires obtaining DR Rating to be reloaded. If you are interrupted while reloading, you must start over."

"Some weapons are almost as likely to hurt you as your opponent. Any failed Test that includes a 9 on the tens or units die results in a Clumsiness (see Chapter 5: Rules for more information on Clumsiness). If this reduces the slot’s AP below 0, the Armor becomes unusable."
"The weapon is tiring to use or difficult to aim with. You only gain the benefits of Concussive and Devastating Weapon Traits in a Turn where you Charge."

"Imprecise weapons are unwieldy because they are heavy or hard to aim with. Take a -1 DR penalty when using the weapon to attack. An Imprecise weapon can never also be Accurate (Imprecise takes precedence)."
"Some weapons are not very good at penetrating armor. All AP is doubled against harmless weapons. In addition, you do not automatically inflict the minimum of 1 Wound on a successful hit in combat."

"Slow weapons are heavy and massive, making them difficult to use properly. Characters using Slow weapons always strike last in a Round, regardless of Initiative order. Additionally, opponents gain a +1 DR bonus to any Checks to defend against your attacks."
"Affected characters are in Ignited state"

"Slashing weapons have heavy blades that can slice through armor with horrifying ease. If you hit an opponent, you Damage a piece of armor or a hit Shield by 1 Point while injuring the target. You still suffer the normal Wounds (and since your AP is now reduced by 1 Point, you probably suffer an additional Wound), but you avoid the effects of the Critical Wound, as the hit is absorbed by your now damaged armor"
"Flexible armor can be worn under a layer of non-Flexible armor if desired. If so, you gain the benefits of both."
"Armor is particularly tough, meaning most attacks simply can’t penetrate it. Any Critical Wounds caused by an odd number to hit you, such as 11 or 33, are ignored."
"The armor does not fully cover the Location. An opponent who rolls an even number to hit you, or gets a Critical Hit, ignores Partial Armor AP."

"The armor has small Weak Points where a blade can easily slip through if your opponent is skilled or lucky enough. If your opponent has a weapon with the Impaler Perk and rolls a Critical, your armor’s APs are ignored."
"Wearing any mesh or flat gives a -10 Stealth penalty each time"
"Wearing this armor grants a -10% penalty to Perception"
"Wearing this armor grants a -20% penalty to Perception"
"It is possible to place this armor under another"
"Wearing that armor gives a -20 Stealth penalty each time"

Sort.Explanation: "Your target can reduce the duration of a disease they are afflicted with by one day. This Prayer can only be attempted once per illness and per person."
" Your target’s weapon is considered Magic."
"Your target gains +10 Dexterity."
"Your target regains +1 Wound Point."
"Your target gains +10 Agility."
"Your target gains +10 Shooting Skill"

"You steal the wind from the sails of a ship or boat. He is completely becalmed. Even in stormy weather, eerily calm and smooth waters surround the ship as fierce winds, blistering rains, and towering ridges rise and crash all around it. This zone of calm extends around the ship for a distance in meters equal to the Initiative Bonus, and if the ship is propelled by another means, such as oars, the zone of calm moves with it."

"You beg Manann to provide you with food. By staying in a body of water, you catch enough fish to feed 1 person; if it’s at sea you get enough for 2 people. For each +2 DR, you can feed another person."

"You call upon Manann to allow you to cross open water as though it were solid ground. This only works on large expanses of at least tenm wide. Anything smaller is too far from Manann’s domain to notice."

"Your target is immediately drenched in salt water, staggering as if on the swaying deck of a stormy ship. Her hair is swept by spectral winds, and the spray lacerates her skin. She gains the Blinded, Deafened and Exhausted States and must make an Accessible (+20) Agility Test to use her Movement. On a miss, it also gains the Downed State."

"The target ship’s sails fill with favorable winds, swiftly carrying it safely to its destination. As long as this Miracle is active, the sailboat moves at its maximum speed, regardless of wind, tide or current. All Tests taken to steer the ship gain a +10 bonus."

"You implore Manann to drown your enemies. Your target’s lungs fill with salt water continuously while Miracle is active. Her hair floats around her head as if submerged. Your target gains the Exhausted State and is subject to the Drowning and Suffocation rules (page 181) while the Miracle is active. When the Miracle ends, your target must make a Hard (-20) Resistance Test. On a failure, it also suffers a Downed State."

"You call upon the power of Morr to smite all undead. A black fire spreads from your body in a perfect circle whose radius in m is equal to your Sociability Bonus. All potential targets with the Undead Creature Trait lose 1d10 Wound Points, which ignore Toughness Bonus and AP. Any undead destroyed by this Miracle can never be raised by Necromancy under normal conditions. For each +2 DR, you can increase the area of effect by +(BATTR_Fel)m."

"Looking deeply into your target’s eyes while whispering a lament to Morr, you gain a vision of his Destiny, a glimpse of what the future holds. This vision is almost always linked to the death of the target. This Miracle can only be performed once per Character, after which the Destiny Talent can be purchased by XP as if it were part of the target’s Career."

"You touch the eyes of someone near death and implore Morr to guide their soul without taking it away. The target must have 0 Wound Points and be willing. For the duration of the Miracle, the target gains the Unconscious State and will not degrade until the Miracle ends, repelling disease, ignoring Critical Wounds, poisons or otherwise. The Miracle ends if proper healing is done, or if you perform the funeral rites. If you do, which takes about a minute, the target’s soul will pass through the Portal to Death, and the corpse can never be used by Necromancy."
"Morr works through you, stepping through the Portal to reveal his presence to your enemies. Your face takes on a cadaverous appearance and you gain Fear 1."

"You sing a solemn requiem in front of a corpse. This Miracle ensures that the soul is sent through the Portal to the Kingdom of Morr, and ensures that the corpse cannot be targeted by Necromancy Spells. If the Miracle targets an enemy with Undead or Crafted Creature Traits, it will be destroyed."

"You draw a line eight meters long on the ground while chanting a dirge to Morr. Upon performing this Miracle, an indistinct dark portal seems to appear amid the hoarse cawing of crows. Creatures with the Undead Creature Trait must pass an Intermediate (+0) Willpower Test to cross the line. Creatures with both Undead and Fabricated Traits simply cannot cross it. The Miracle remains active until dawn."
"Your passionate prayers inspire your allies with fierce contempt for their enemies. All affected allies gain the Psychic Trait Hatred towards anyone who engages them in combat."
"Your passionate prayers incite Myrmidia to shield your allies with wisps of bright, flickering light, repelling enemy strikes. All affected targets gain +1 AP at all Locations."
"Your Uplifting Prayers inspire discipline and coordination within your ranks. Affected targets gain +1 Elbow Talent."
"If you wield a spear, it gains the Percussive Perk, and is considered Magical."

"You call on Myrmidia to send a Divine Servant, granting you knowledge of your enemies. A spectral eagle manifests, hovering in the sky above. The eagle looks and has the abilities of a normal eagle, but cannot physically affect the world, or be harmed in any way. While the Miracle is active, you can see through the eagle’s eyes and control its flight, surveying the battlefield and spying on your enemies. Your vision is sharp, but you don’t have access to any of your own Talents, such as Night Vision. While you look through the eyes of the eagle, you cannot do so through your own eyes, which leaves you potentially vulnerable."

"You call upon Myrmidia to clear the battlefield of disreputable foes, causing a blinding flash of golden light to erupt. All non-Myrmidians looking your way receive 1 Blinded State. For each +2 DR, they receive +1 Blinded State."
"You call on Ranald to allow your target to navigate the puzzles of reality. Your target gains +10 Agility, +10 Stealth and +1 Feline Flexibility Talent for the duration of the Miracle."

"You state one of Ranald’s riddles about portals, whether or not they exist when closed. One of the locking systems of a door, a window or a targeted hatch gives way: a lock is unlocked, a latch is released, a rope is detached. For each +2 DR, you can target another door, window, or hatch locking system."

" Crossing your fingers, you ask Ranald’s riddle and ask what exactly is luck? Gain +1 Luck Point. For each +2 DR, you can gain an additional +1 Luck Point, which can go beyond the normal maximum. You can no longer invoke this Miracle until you have reached 0 Luck Points."

"Smiling at Ranald while cheekily asking others what exactly wealth is? For each affected target, choose an option: » The target’s purse appears empty. Target’s purse seems full. Target’s outfit looks cheap and insignificant. The target’s attire appears rich and well-tailored. The only valuable object available is impossible to collect. For each +2 DR, you may choose an additional effect for one of your targets."

"You state a complex riddle concerning the reality of that which cannot be perceived. Targets affected by this Miracle can go unnoticed, provided they do not draw attention to themselves by touching, attacking, calling someone, casting a Spell, or making noise. You can summon this Miracle only if no one is looking directly at you."

"Is there anything that cannot be seen? You pose the riddle to Ranald, who responds with a Divine Servant in the form of a cat. This envoy looks and has the abilities of a normal cat, but cannot be harmed in any way. While the Miracle is active, you perceive everything the cat perceives — what it sees, hears, touches — and you control its Movement. Your senses are sharp as a cat’s, but you don’t have access to any of your own Talents, such as Night Vision. While the Miracle is active, you cannot perceive anything through your own senses, which leaves you vulnerable."

"You sing one of the anthems about shelter and safety in Rhya. You can only invoke this Miracle outdoors and outside populated areas. You discover a perfect natural shelter. A combination of earth and trees formed an ideal place to camp for the night. The area is protected from all natural rains and winds and lasts as long as you camp there. The shelter is large enough for one person. For each +2 DR, it allows an additional individual. When you leave the camp, the shelter cannot be rediscovered. As if its existence was only due to the will of your goddess."

"You place your hands on a wounded or sick target while chanting your Prayers. Choose one of the following effects: - Heal (BATTR_Fel) Wounds. - Treat 1 disease contracted naturally. For each +2 DR, you can choose another effect, or the same one repeatedly. This Miracle is slow, and results take at least 10 minutes to show up. If interrupted, the Miracle will need to be invoked again."

"Put your hands down, you chant a Prayer for Rhya asking for her help to better understand her Kingdom. This Miracle can only be summoned outdoors, outside of populated areas.
